title: Zcash Turns 10 as Grayscale Highlights Its 20% Developer Fund
summary: Zcash will mark its 10th anniversary on Oct. 28 with a decade of protocol upgrades behind it. Grayscale says one reason the privacy-focused crypto network has kept evolving is its unusual decision to direct 20% of block rewards toward developer and ecosystem funding. Zcash’s 20% Dev Fund Sets It Apa...
content:
Zcash will mark its 10th anniversary on Oct. 28 with a decade of protocol upgrades behind it. Grayscale says one reason the privacy-focused crypto network has kept evolving is its unusual decision to direct 20% of block rewards toward developer and ecosystem funding.

Key Takeaways

  • Zcash turns 10 on Oct. 28, with 20% of block rewards funding development and ecosystem grants.
  • Sprout, Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood show how protocol funding has sustained technical upgrades.
  • Its next decade will hinge on keeping privacy secure against quantum and AI-driven threats.

Zcash’s 20% Dev Fund Sets It Apart From Bitcoin

Zcash is turning 10 with a development model that looks very different from Bitcoin’s.

Grayscale highlighted the network’s built-in funding structure ahead of the anniversary, arguing that Zcash’s ability to keep shipping technical upgrades through multiple crypto cycles has been supported by protocol-level funding for research and development.

Currently, miners receive 80% of ZEC block rewards, while 20% is allocated to development-related programs.

That structure has given Zcash a recurring source of funding rather than leaving development entirely dependent on venture capital or private donations.

Zcash Funding Model Faces a New Proposal

The current Dev Fund sends 8% of block rewards to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), and another 12% to the Coinholder-Controlled funding mechanism.

But that structure could soon change.

Zcash co-founder and protocol developer Sean Bowe has submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal that would end the 8% block subsidy going to ZCG and redirect it to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM).

Rather than entering immediate circulation, those ZEC would be withheld under the proposed mechanism.

Bowe argues that ZCG already has sufficient reserves to continue funding grants. The proposal would leave ZCG’s existing treasury untouched, while also preserving the separate 12% allocation, miners’ share of block rewards, and ZEC’s maximum supply.

The debate highlights how Zcash’s funding model continues to evolve alongside the technology it supports.

Privacy Pools Show a Decade of Iteration

Zcash’s clearest technical progress has come through its shielded pools.

The network launched with Sprout, followed by Sapling in 2018 and Orchard in 2022. In 2026, the Ironwood upgrade addressed a code vulnerability while introducing quantum-recoverable addresses and formal verification.

Formal verification uses mathematical methods to establish whether software satisfies specified security properties, an increasingly relevant safeguard for privacy infrastructure.

Each generation has effectively rebuilt parts of Zcash’s privacy architecture rather than leaving its original design untouched.

Post-Quantum Security Is the Next Test

Grayscale expects future development to focus increasingly on transaction capacity, post-quantum preparedness, and cybersecurity risks amplified by artificial intelligence.

That matters because privacy-focused crypto faces an unusually demanding security challenge. The network must protect both users’ funds and the confidentiality of their transactions.

Zcash’s anniversary therefore arrives at an important moment.

After a decade of protocol-funded development, the question is no longer simply whether that model can finance innovation. It is how Zcash should allocate those resources as its priorities shift toward quantum security, sustainability, and the next generation of privacy technology.

title: Bithumb discloses data leak after internal system breach: Report
summary: The breach impacted its in-house mobile system, used by employees for work and information sharing.
content:
South Korea’s crypto exchange Bithumb is investigating the extent of a data leak caused by a hack of its internal mobile system earlier this week, Yonhap News Agency reported Wednesday.

Bithumb discovered the breach of its in-house mobile system — the platform used by employees to communicate internally — on Tuesday and notified the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission that day, according to Yonhap, which cited industry sources.

The exchange is investigating the scope of the attack, including whether member data was leaked.

“We are analyzing the exact scope, including the possibility of member information being involved,” Bithumb told Yonhap. “We will provide an official announcement this morning. However, the internal work system is separated from the virtual asset trading system, so customer virtual assets cannot be accessed through this breach.”

Cointelegraph reached out to Bithumb for further comment.

The incident adds to a recent wave of cyberattacks in Korea’s financial sector.

During a meeting at the Financial Supervisory Authority headquarters on Wednesday, Governor Lee Chan-jin said cyberattacks had hit 16 South Korean financial firms as of Oct. 14.

The Korea Times reports that asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities were also recent victims of cyberattacks.

Daishin Securities said that personal and credit information belonging to 38,490 customers had been leaked. Mirae Asset Global Investments said it had blocked abnormal external access to some web systems and was investigating the incident. The company said investor information was not affected, according to Yonhap.

Related: Bithumb sets 2028 IPO timetable as it overhauls internal controls

title: HashKey Launches First hToken Linked to Investment Fund Units
summary: HashKey RWA announced on October 26 that it had launched the first product in its hToken series, linked to Class A units of HashKey Fintech Opportunities.
content:
TL;DR: HashKey RWA announced on October 26 that it had launched the first product in its hToken series, linked to Class A units of HashKey Fintech Opportunities Limited. Watch for additional hToken issuances, their asset types, legal rights, distribution channels and evidence of real investor participation.

The latest development in HashKey’s corner of the digital-asset market is worth examining beyond the headline. A 2026-10-26 announcement describes a concrete change, but the investment consequences will depend on how it works in practice. The original record is available in the original company statement; here is what it establishes, why the distinction matters and what remains unproven.

What the source actually says

HashKey RWA announced on October 26 that it had launched the first product in its hToken series, linked to Class A units of HashKey Fintech Opportunities Limited. The company describes hToken as a repeatable structure for issuing tokenised securities and handling their lifecycle, rather than another general-purpose cryptocurrency. The underlying reference is an investment fund, and the token’s rights must be assessed through its own documentation; holding a representation of exposure should not be assumed to mean holding legal title to a fund unit.

HashKey’s stated objective is to make token issuance less bespoke for traditional financial institutions. In practice, moving assets onto a ledger often requires the same work every time: determining ownership rights, verifying permitted investors, arranging custody, setting transfer restrictions and providing reliable reports. A standardised issuance approach could shorten some of this preparation. However, it cannot abolish the legal differences between funds, markets and jurisdictions, nor can it substitute for checking the specific terms of each series.

The first product uses HashKey’s asset-management and trading connections and has been presented for eligible professional investors. Access through a digital-asset platform may alter how subscriptions or subsequent transactions are processed, but investor eligibility remains central. The announcement sits at the junction of fund distribution and blockchain infrastructure, not retail token speculation. Any statement about returns would need to come from the relevant fund documentation and cannot be inferred merely because the product is tradable using stablecoin infrastructure.

For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. The underlying development can strengthen a company’s product, legal position or operating capacity without determining what a token will trade for tomorrow. The linked source establishes what was disclosed; the valuation question requires a separate assessment of customers, costs, execution and market conditions. That gap between a confirmed fact and a forecast is where much of the investment risk sits.

What matters for the market next

HashKey’s commercial challenge is to prove that other managers will adopt the structure rather than build one-off systems or retain existing registrars. Reusability is valuable only when it reduces complexity for each participant in the chain. Compliance controls, transfer-agency records and clear redemption processes remain the foundations. Investors should be wary of conflating high transaction speed with liquidity in the underlying fund, as the latter depends on asset characteristics and counterparties.

Watch for additional hToken issuances, their asset types, legal rights, distribution channels and evidence of real investor participation. The launch signals an effort to industrialise tokenisation, but one initial product cannot establish the economics of a scalable issuance network. The most persuasive result would be repeat deployments that preserve legal certainty and operating discipline while genuinely lowering costs for issuers and holders.

Market watchers should also avoid treating a company’s or regulator’s headline as a substitute for terms and conditions. Tokens, shares and regulated service agreements create different rights, even when they coexist in one wallet or platform. A reliable follow-up should ask which entity is responsible, what a holder can actually redeem or transfer, and whether the claimed advantages appear in live activity. Those questions are more informative than an unsupported price target or an assumption that adoption is inevitable.

Primary source: original company statement (2026-10-26).

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: OG.com and Crypto.com Launch 24/7 Crypto Perpetuals for US Traders
summary: Crypto.com and OG.com have opened the door to perpetual crypto derivatives for eligible U.S. traders, introducing contracts that never expire and offer up to five times leverage through a federally regulated trading structure accessible to retail and institutional customers. Crypto.com Expands U.S. ...
content:
Crypto.com and OG.com have opened the door to perpetual crypto derivatives for eligible U.S. traders, introducing contracts that never expire and offer up to five times leverage through a federally regulated trading structure accessible to retail and institutional customers.

Key Takeaways

  • Crypto.com and OG.com launched regulated crypto perpetuals for eligible U.S. traders on Oct. 27.
  • Crypto.com’s new contracts offer up to 5x leverage without expiration dates.
  • OG.com’s regulated infrastructure supports trading through the Crypto.com App and Exchange.

Crypto.com Expands U.S. Derivatives Access With 24/7 Trading

On Tuesday, OG.com and Crypto.com announced the launch of crypto perpetual contracts across the Crypto.com App and Crypto.com Exchange, extending leveraged digital asset trading to eligible U.S. customers through a Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-regulated framework.

The rollout follows Crypto.com’s registration as an introducing broker with the National Futures Association. OG.com operates a CFTC-regulated exchange, clearinghouse and futures commission merchant, establishing the infrastructure supporting the new offering.

Unlike conventional futures contracts, which expire on predetermined dates, perpetual derivatives allow traders to maintain positions indefinitely, provided they satisfy applicable margin requirements.

The contracts support long and short positions, up to 5x leverage, isolated margin, and take-profit and stop-loss orders. Retail customers can access the products through Crypto.com’s mobile application, while institutional and experienced traders receive access through its exchange.

From Offshore Trading Floors to Regulated U.S. Markets

Perpetual futures have a curious history in the land of crypto derivatives. Economist Robert Shiller proposed the underlying concept in 1993, but cryptocurrency exchanges eventually transformed it into one of the industry’s busiest trading instruments.

Bitmex helped popularize the modern crypto perpetual swap in May 2016, introducing its XBTUSD contract with leverage reaching 100x. The instrument eliminated the recurring headache of rolling expiring futures positions into new contracts.

Perpetuals typically rely on funding payments between long and short traders to keep contract prices aligned with underlying spot markets. When contracts trade above their reference prices, longs generally compensate shorts. The reverse occurs when contracts trade below those benchmarks.

The arrangement supports continuous speculation and hedging, although funding expenses and margin requirements can quickly complicate leveraged positions. Crypto.com’s U.S. offering limits leverage to 5x, considerably below the 20x to 100x exposure available on numerous international cryptocurrency derivatives platforms.

Crypto.com Targets Retail and Institutional Traders

Kris Marszalek, founder and CEO of OG.com and Crypto.com, described the launch as another step toward consolidating financial products within a single trading environment. “Whether hedging a crypto portfolio or capitalizing on 24/7 price action, our traders now have direct access to continuous liquidity, flexible leverage, and built-in risk controls,” Marszalek said.

The companies intend to integrate perpetual derivatives alongside existing spot cryptocurrency services, prediction markets and rewards offerings. For crypto traders, the appeal is straightforward: positions can remain open without expiration, and leverage allows larger market exposure with less initial collateral. Yet liquidation remains a possibility when adverse price movements exhaust available margin.

The launch also reflects a broader migration of perpetual-style derivatives from offshore cryptocurrency exchanges into regulated American financial infrastructure. An instrument once associated primarily with overseas trading venues is now competing for customers inside the U.S. regulatory perimeter.

title: Coinbase Converts GYEN Balances to USDC as Stablecoin Winds Down
summary: Coinbase has told customers that support for the yen-linked GYEN stablecoin is being wound down as its issuer, GMO-Z.com Trust Company, retires the.
content:
TL;DR: Coinbase has told customers that support for the yen-linked GYEN stablecoin is being wound down as its issuer, GMO-Z.com Trust Company, retires the product. The status notice is the relevant primary communication for Coinbase customers, and its time window needs to be read precisely.

The latest development in Coinbase’s corner of the digital-asset market is worth examining beyond the headline. A 2026-10-26 announcement describes a concrete change, but the investment consequences will depend on how it works in practice. The original record is available in the original company statement; here is what it establishes, why the distinction matters and what remains unproven.

What the source actually says

Coinbase has told customers that support for the yen-linked GYEN stablecoin is being wound down as its issuer, GMO-Z.com Trust Company, retires the product. According to Coinbase’s status notice, sending and receiving GYEN on the platform was disabled from October 26, 2026, and remaining customer balances are scheduled for conversion into USDC between October 26 and October 30. The conversion is at the prevailing market rate when it happens, not at a universal promised yen-dollar parity.

The exchange says it will not charge a transaction fee for the conversion. However, a no-fee exchange does not mean that the user receives a fixed economic outcome, because GYEN and USDC refer to different currencies and the conversion rate can move. Customers who wanted to retain GYEN had an earlier withdrawal window. Once the process finishes, Coinbase says it will no longer support GYEN deposits or withdrawals, warning that unsupported deposits might not be recoverable.

This is a reminder that the lifespan of a token depends on more than its blockchain. Issuers can discontinue products, exchanges can end transfers and payment applications can change which units they support. Stablecoins are often discussed as permanent digital representations of currency, yet practical usability relies on banks, compliance programmes, redemption arrangements and secondary venues. A user holding a token privately may face different options from someone keeping it on a custodial exchange.

For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. The underlying development can strengthen a company’s product, legal position or operating capacity without determining what a token will trade for tomorrow. The linked source establishes what was disclosed; the valuation question requires a separate assessment of customers, costs, execution and market conditions. That gap between a confirmed fact and a forecast is where much of the investment risk sits.

What matters for the market next

There are also important distinctions between a token being technically transferable and being accepted by a particular service. Even where onchain transfers remain possible, liquidity and conversion into a bank balance can be constrained. Exchanges must explain operational cutoffs clearly, especially when a product is connected to a non-dollar currency. For affected holders, transaction records and the applicable conversion value may also matter for financial reporting or tax.

The status notice is the relevant primary communication for Coinbase customers, and its time window needs to be read precisely. The prudent next step for an affected customer is to inspect completed conversions and retain the exchange record rather than send additional GYEN to a disabled deposit address. The episode illustrates a broader infrastructure question for stablecoins: who keeps access working when an issuer decides that a token’s commercial life is over?

Market watchers should also avoid treating a company’s or regulator’s headline as a substitute for terms and conditions. Tokens, shares and regulated service agreements create different rights, even when they coexist in one wallet or platform. A reliable follow-up should ask which entity is responsible, what a holder can actually redeem or transfer, and whether the claimed advantages appear in live activity. Those questions are more informative than an unsupported price target or an assumption that adoption is inevitable.

Primary source: original company statement (2026-10-26).

title: Discord is making public chats searchable on Google: How to opt out
summary: Discord conversations on large public servers will soon reach audiences far beyond their communities, raising privacy concerns.
content:
Discord is making a policy change that will make conversations from its largest public servers discoverable in search engines, including Google, raising privacy concerns among users whose conversations were previously confined to the platform. 

The change applies to Discoverable Servers — communities with at least 1,000 members listed in Discord’s public directory that do not require an invitation to join. 

From Nov. 16, every Discoverable Server will have a web page that may include summaries of public channel discussions. From mid-December, individual messages posted in eligible channels may appear in web search, Discord said Tuesday. Messages posted before the rollout will not be included, while usernames and avatars will be excluded from published messages. 

Discord said the shift of online communities from message boards to its servers had made useful answers harder to find. “This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this,” the company said.

The move has drawn criticism from users concerned about their conversations reaching an audience outside of their intended community, even if the servers are public in the first place. 

Related: Starknet introduces wallet privacy feature for DeFi activity

Others welcomed the change, saying it could make useful answers easier to find. One user in Discord’s announcement thread called it “very much necessary,” while another said moving communities from forums to Discord had made their discussions harder to find through search.

The change could also affect cryptocurrency communities that use Discord for technical discussions, support and project announcements.

Cointelegraph found nearly 800 servers tagged “cryptocurrency,” around 1,400 tagged “trading” and more than 700 tagged “finance” in Discord’s public directory. Discord said there are over 63,000 total discoverable servers on its platform. 

How to opt out 

Users have until the message-sharing rollout begins in mid-December to opt out before their posts become eligible to appear online. Discord said the feature will be disabled by default for users in Australia, the EU, the European Economic Area, the UK, Canada, Brazil and South Korea. Teen users will also be excluded.

To opt out, users should go into User Settings > Data & Privacy and switch off “Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages.” The setting covers every Discoverable Server a user belongs to, according to Discord’s guidance.

Users can also disable the feature after launch, but it only protects messages sent after the opt-out. Users who want an eligible message removed must delete it from Discord, and Discord warns that search engines may retain cached copies for some time.

Server administrators can also prevent messages from individual channels or entire servers from appearing on public web pages and in search results through Server Settings > Web Presence.

They can separately disable discussion summaries, which are scheduled to begin rolling out in November.

title: Bitcoin Eyes $125K as Galaxy Says Bear Market Has Ended
summary: Galaxy sees favorable conditions for bitcoin to retake $125,000, arguing that its bear market ended in June and selling pressure has diminished. Its analysis also cited fiscal pressures and weak investor attention to support its bullish outlook. Galaxy Sees Favorable Setup for $125K Bitcoin Bitcoin ...
content:
Galaxy sees favorable conditions for bitcoin to retake $125,000, arguing that its bear market ended in June and selling pressure has diminished. Its analysis also cited fiscal pressures and weak investor attention to support its bullish outlook.

Key Takeaways

  • Galaxy identified favorable conditions for bitcoin to retake $125,000.
  • The firm concluded that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June.
  • Galaxy linked the accumulation phase to patterns preceding past advances.

Galaxy Sees Favorable Setup for $125K Bitcoin

Bitcoin had a favorable setup for retaking $125,000, Galaxy argued in research published Oct. 26 after it was sent to clients Oct. 22. Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at the digital asset financial services company, based the case for bitcoin’s recovery on reduced selling pressure and resilient investor demand.

At the time of writing, bitcoin traded at $80,762.07 on Bitstamp, up 1.09% over the previous 24 hours. Thorn stated:

“Bitcoin has proven its ability to run to at least $125K, and we see no reason why it can’t retake that level, and indeed the setup looks favorable.”

His assessment placed the recovery within a broader market transition. Thorn added: “We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance.”

Recovery Signals Meet a Shift in Ownership

An August study had identified the 50-week moving average as a recovery threshold. Galaxy’s October analysis highlighted four historical recoveries following at least 20 weeks below that average. Each regained its prior all-time high within 33-83 weeks.

September supplied that technical milestone when bitcoin crossed $84,000 after regaining its 50-week average. Through Oct. 18, it had recorded five consecutive weekly closes above the average after spending 44 weeks below it.

Onchain indicators reinforced the assessment: the 53% maximum drawdown was shallower than earlier bear markets, while bitcoin remained above the network’s aggregate onchain cost basis. Short-term holders were approximately 9% above their average acquisition cost, without substantial profit-taking.

In July, Ki Young Ju, CEO of blockchain analytics firm Cryptoquant, said ETF and corporate buyers were absorbing older holders’ sales. Galaxy subsequently found that spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) added 87,000 BTC after the June low.

Institutional demand persisted despite trading firms retreating: nine firms reduced ETF exposure by 68,000 BTC, while other reporting institutions collectively added 20,000 BTC between September 2025 and June 2026. Monthly movement of coins dormant for at least five years fell to 34,000 BTC so far in 2026 from 67,000 BTC in 2024.

Debt Supports the Thesis as Risks Remain

Government borrowing strengthened Thorn’s argument for an asset with predetermined issuance. Under the network’s shared validation rules, bitcoin’s issuance is limited to approximately 21 million coins. His assessment cited $40.44 trillion in federal debt, a $1.99 trillion annual deficit, and Morgan Stanley’s expected $570 billion in AI-related debt issuance during 2026.

Investor attention favored stablecoins and tokenization, resembling earlier periods when institutions embraced blockchain applications while overlooking bitcoin. Stablecoin supply had expanded 129% since early 2024 to $304 billion, which Thorn viewed as capital remaining within crypto.

Potential setbacks included AI competition for investment capital, AI-assisted theft, a technology downturn affecting risk assets, and future quantum computing vulnerabilities. Galaxy also highlighted defensive upgrades and industry funding.

Thorn concluded:

“We believe the bottom is in, selling pressure has diminished, the debasement case has strengthened, and the crowd has left: these are all reasons we remain bullish on bitcoin.”

The assessment would weaken following a weekly close below the 50-week average, valued at $76,540 in the Oct. 22 analysis, without recovery within a month. Other triggers included ETF holdings below 1.22 million BTC, credible timing for a quantum computer capable of breaking Bitcoin’s cryptography, or U.S. fiscal consolidation.

title: AI Stocks Boom as MEXC Tokenized Trading Volume Jumps 88%
summary: MEXC experienced significant growth across its traditional finance offerings, with trading volume for AI-related assets rising 88% month-over-month. AI Trading Volume Expands Across Peripheral Sectors Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC reported significant growth across its traditional finance product sui...
content:
MEXC experienced significant growth across its traditional finance offerings, with trading volume for AI-related assets rising 88% month-over-month.

Key Takeaways

  • In September, MEXC saw AI asset spot volume surge 88% and tokenized U.S. stock spot volume jump 81%.
  • Hardware demand surged as semiconductor derivatives generated 77% of top 10 futures volume on MEXC.
  • CEO Vugar Usi noted MEXC will continually adapt platform products as AI demand expands past chips.

AI Trading Volume Expands Across Peripheral Sectors

Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC reported significant growth across its traditional finance product suite for September, driven by heightened demand for artificial intelligence (AI) assets and semiconductor-focused derivatives.

Trading volume for tokenized U.S. stock spot products increased 81% month over month, while overall volume for AI-related assets grew 88%. Meanwhile, Pre-IPO Futures trading volume surged 60%, and semiconductor and memory assets accounted for 77% of the total volume among the top 10 Stock and Index Futures.

According to data released by the exchange, trading volume in AI-related assets outpaced the 63% growth registered by non-AI assets in September. AI-linked products represented 48% of total tokenized U.S. stock and exchange-traded fund (ETF) spot trading volume on the platform, up from 44% in August.

Investor interest broadened beyond chipmakers to include peripheral infrastructure, such as power equipment and optical networking. Four specific subsectors posted monthly growth above 90%, led by semiconductors and memory, which rose 100%. Optical communications and networking jumped 99%, power and energy equipment rose 96%, and computing infrastructure and data centers grew 91%.

Meanwhile, the data show AI companies claimed six of the top 10 positions for most-traded tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs, generating 59% of the combined volume for that group. Crypto-related firms secured the remaining four spots, accounting for 41%. Within the top 10, assets linked to AI cloud services, chip design, and data center infrastructure jointly held a 38% share of volume.

Hardware Manufacturers Lead Derivatives Trading

Derivatives trading remained heavily concentrated in hardware manufacturers. Semiconductor and memory assets held five of the top 10 positions by futures trading volume, representing 77% of the total among the top tier. Micron Technology, SK Hynix and Sandisk Corp. took the top three spots, generating 67% of the top 10 volume combined. The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares ETF and Nvidia Corp. also placed within the top 10.

MEXC, meanwhile, expanded its listed asset base during the month, increasing its traditional finance futures trading pairs by 15%. Pre-IPO futures emerged as the fastest-growing category with a 60% increase in trading volume, while Japanese stock futures grew 47%. The exchange also added a dedicated listing section for Taiwanese equities.

Among Pre-IPO contracts, Moonshot AI trading volume rose 115% month over month, Enflame gained 99%, and OpenAI grew 51%. The platform expanded its private market listings in September by introducing Pre-IPO futures for prediction platform Polymarket, memory maker YMTC, and health technology firm Oura.

The exchange currently supports more than 450 stock and index futures pairs, over 200 tokenized U.S. equities, and access to more than 7,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs via its RealStocks offering.

“September’s data show that demand for AI-related trading is expanding beyond chips into the broader value chain,” said MEXC Chief Executive Officer Vugar Usi. “For trading platforms, the challenge is not simply to expand asset coverage, but to adapt to users’ evolving trading needs.”

title: Hong Kong Opens 24/7 Trading for Two Tokenised Money-Market Funds
summary: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission announced on October 26 that it had approved secondary trading for two existing authorised tokenised.
content:
TL;DR: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission announced on October 26 that it had approved secondary trading for two existing authorised tokenised money-market funds on a licensed virtual-asset platform. The regulator says it will monitor trading and consider whether to expand eligible products.

The latest development in Hong’s corner of the digital-asset market is worth examining beyond the headline. A 2026-10-26 announcement describes a concrete change, but the investment consequences will depend on how it works in practice. The original record is available in the original company statement; here is what it establishes, why the distinction matters and what remains unproven.

What the source actually says

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission announced on October 26 that it had approved secondary trading for two existing authorised tokenised money-market funds on a licensed virtual-asset platform. The products are ChinaAMC’s Hong Kong-dollar and US-dollar digital money-market funds, with trading available around the clock. The key development is not simply that fund interests exist in token form: it is that investors can now trade those interests with one another in a regulated secondary-market environment outside the usual dealing window.

Secondary trading means a buyer and seller can exchange existing units without every transaction requiring a subscription or redemption directly with the fund. That can make positions easier to move when the underlying money markets are closed. But a quoted secondary-market price may diverge from the fund’s net asset value, and sufficient liquidity depends on active buyers, sellers and market makers. A blockchain token does not remove those familiar market risks, even if transfers occur very quickly.

The SFC introduced a pilot framework in April 2026 covering the operation of this trading channel, fair pricing, liquidity provision and disclosures. The approval applies to specified products within that framework; it should not be read as blanket permission for all tokenised investments to trade continuously. Hong Kong is building regulatory infrastructure step by step, tying new market activity to existing authorised funds and licensed trading platforms rather than treating every token as interchangeable.

For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. The underlying development can strengthen a company’s product, legal position or operating capacity without determining what a token will trade for tomorrow. The linked source establishes what was disclosed; the valuation question requires a separate assessment of customers, costs, execution and market conditions. That gap between a confirmed fact and a forecast is where much of the investment risk sits.

What matters for the market next

For asset managers, around-the-clock access creates opportunities and new obligations. Investors in different time zones may want to rebalance cash products at weekends, while platforms must continue surveillance, reference pricing and customer protection beyond exchange opening hours. An operational advantage on the trading side also depends on how cash proceeds are settled and transferred back into conventional accounts. Settlement arrangements are as important as the existence of a 24-hour order book.

The regulator says it will monitor trading and consider whether to expand eligible products. The practical measures to watch are spreads, price deviations, market depth, volume and evidence that redemption mechanisms can support investor confidence. The decision is a significant Hong Kong experiment in regulated tokenisation, but it is best evaluated as a defined market-structure pilot rather than proof that every mutual fund can instantly become a liquid digital token.

Market watchers should also avoid treating a company’s or regulator’s headline as a substitute for terms and conditions. Tokens, shares and regulated service agreements create different rights, even when they coexist in one wallet or platform. A reliable follow-up should ask which entity is responsible, what a holder can actually redeem or transfer, and whether the claimed advantages appear in live activity. Those questions are more informative than an unsupported price target or an assumption that adoption is inevitable.

title: Galaxy Digital Shares Rise Following $323M Q3 Profit, New $200M Buyback Plan
summary: Galaxy Digital returned to profitability in the third quarter of 2026, reporting $323 million in net income as gains from its investment portfolio and rapid growth in its AI data center business helped offset continued losses in its core digital assets division. Shares were up on Tuesday following t...
content:
Galaxy Digital returned to profitability in the third quarter of 2026, reporting $323 million in net income as gains from its investment portfolio and rapid growth in its AI data center business helped offset continued losses in its core digital assets division. Shares were up on Tuesday following the announcement.

Key Takeaways

  • Galaxy Digital returned to profitability in Q3 2026, reporting $323 million in net income and $455 million in adjusted EBITDA, driven largely by investment gains and AI infrastructure growth.
  • AI data center profits surged, with adjusted gross profit nearly quadrupling to $79 million as Galaxy expanded its Texas facilities and pursued additional capacity.
  • Galaxy authorized another $200 million share buyback after completing its previous $200 million program, while total assets climbed 51% to $16.4 billion.

The Mike Novogratz-led cryptocurrency investment firm reported Tuesday that it earned $323 million during the three months ended Sept. 30, reversing an $85 million loss in the second quarter. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) reached $455 million, compared with a $77 million loss in the previous quarter.

Galaxy reported adjusted gross profit of $569 million, up sharply from $43 million in the second quarter. Diluted earnings per share reached $0.66, while adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.83.

“Galaxy delivered a strong third quarter, reflecting the strength of our established digital assets franchise, significant appreciation across our investments portfolio, and the growing contribution from our data centers business,” Novogratz said in the earnings announcement.

The company’s treasury and corporate division accounted for much of the improvement, generating $419 million in adjusted gross profit, compared with a $42 million loss in the previous quarter. The segment benefited from appreciation across Galaxy’s investments portfolio.

Meanwhile, its digital assets business generated $71 million in adjusted gross profit, up 9% from the previous quarter, although it still recorded a $9 million adjusted EBITDA loss.

Cryptocurrency trading volumes increased 12% quarter over quarter, outperforming a broader spot market that experienced declining volumes. Galaxy’s average loan book grew 27% to $1.8 billion, while combined assets under management and assets under stake climbed 46% to $10.4 billion.

The company’s expanding institutional cryptocurrency operations included an August partnership with BNY to bring staking services to the banking giant’s digital asset custody platform. As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, the arrangement is designed to let eligible institutional clients earn staking rewards while maintaining their assets within BNY’s existing custody infrastructure.

AI Data Center Expansion Accelerates

Galaxy’s data center division emerged as a significant growth driver during the quarter, generating $79 million in adjusted gross profit, nearly quadrupling the $20 million recorded in the second quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $69 million from $11 million.

The increase reflected the first full quarter of revenue-generating operations under the company’s lease with AI infrastructure provider CoreWeave at its Helios campus in Texas. Galaxy delivered all 133 megawatts of critical IT load associated with the first phase by the end of June.

Galaxy also completed a $3.5 billion senior secured debt offering to finance the second phase of Helios I, which is under construction. The company expects to begin delivering additional data halls in the second quarter of 2027.

Galaxy said it is pursuing potential tenants for another 830 megawatts of approved capacity at Helios II that remains unleased. Its total gross power development pipeline has expanded to more than 5.7 gigawatts.

The expansion follows Galaxy’s July acquisition of approximately 500 acres in McGregor, Texas, for another AI and high-performance computing campus. As Bitcoin.com News reported at the time, the project initially targets 74 megawatts of capacity, with the potential for significantly larger development in subsequent years.

Galaxy has increasingly redirected its infrastructure investments toward AI computing, including converting its former bitcoin mining operations at Helios to serve demand from technology companies.

Galaxy Authorizes Another $200 Million Stock Buyback

Alongside its earnings announcement, Galaxy disclosed that its board had approved an additional $200 million share repurchase program on Oct. 26.

The new authorization follows completion of an earlier $200 million buyback program on Oct. 15, under which Galaxy repurchased approximately 9.8 million shares. Bitcoin.com News covered the original authorization in February, when the company introduced the initiative following a fourth-quarter loss.

Galaxy ended September with $16.4 billion in total assets, up 51% from the previous quarter, and $3 billion in total equity. Its holdings of cash, stablecoins, and U.S. Treasury securities nearly doubled to $4.9 billion from $2.5 billion.

The results mark a significant turnaround after a difficult start to 2026, as Galaxy reported a $216 million first-quarter loss amid declining cryptocurrency prices. The third-quarter rebound underscores Galaxy’s growing reliance on two distinct businesses: cryptocurrency financial services and AI computing infrastructure.

Galaxy shares on the Nasdaq (GLXY) rose following the earnings announcement, finishing the trading day up more than 9.5% at a price of $17.18. Shares in the firm have fallen approximately 23% since the start of the year.

title: Bitmine Says ETH Treasury Exceeds Six Million Coins
summary: Bitmine Immersion Technologies filed an October 26 update with the SEC and said its Ethereum holdings had reached approximately 6.05 million ETH. Its.
content:
TL;DR: Bitmine Immersion Technologies filed an October 26 update with the SEC and said its Ethereum holdings had reached approximately 6.05 million ETH. Future filings can help separate changes attributable to new purchases, staking rewards, token prices and financing or repurchases.

The latest development in Bitmine’s corner of the digital-asset market is worth examining beyond the headline. A 2026-10-26 filing describes a concrete change, but the investment consequences will depend on how it works in practice. The original record is available in the regulatory filing; here is what it establishes, why the distinction matters and what remains unproven.

What the source actually says

Bitmine Immersion Technologies filed an October 26 update with the SEC and said its Ethereum holdings had reached approximately 6.05 million ETH. Its accompanying release put combined crypto, cash, marketable securities and other investments at about $15 billion as of the stated measurement period. These are company-supplied snapshots, rather than real-time portfolio values. Ether’s market price can change rapidly, so the monetary figure may move even if the number of tokens remains unchanged.

The company said it had added 10,452 ETH during the week and estimated that its holdings amounted to about 4.95 percent of the asset’s circulating supply. It also reported 5,227,037 ETH staked through its MAVAN platform and staking partners. Staking introduces a second dimension to a crypto treasury. Instead of solely holding a volatile asset, the company participates in Ethereum’s validator economy and takes on operational exposure, lockup considerations and protocol-dependent reward and penalty mechanics.

Bitmine’s release also discusses share repurchases and cash reserves. These details matter because holders of public company stock do not own a straightforward claim to a fixed number of ETH tokens. They own equity in an enterprise with managers, expenses, capital allocation decisions and potentially changing securities outstanding. The share price may reflect investor sentiment, premiums or discounts to asset values and beliefs about future operations rather than merely multiplying ETH held by a spot quote.

For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. The underlying development can strengthen a company’s product, legal position or operating capacity without determining what a token will trade for tomorrow. The linked source establishes what was disclosed; the valuation question requires a separate assessment of customers, costs, execution and market conditions. That gap between a confirmed fact and a forecast is where much of the investment risk sits.

What matters for the market next

Concentration of this scale makes governance and custody especially important. Asset security, withdrawal controls, validator uptime, market liquidity and counterparties can affect outcomes that a simple treasury chart conceals. A large staking position may produce rewards, but it also needs disciplined systems for accounting and tax treatment. Investors should not assume that published staking valuations are an unconditional cash balance available for distribution to shareholders.

Future filings can help separate changes attributable to new purchases, staking rewards, token prices and financing or repurchases. The most useful metric may be the evolving exposure for each common share, compared with liabilities and cash needs. Bitmine’s latest report confirms continuing concentration in Ethereum; it does not guarantee a favourable outcome for the company if ether declines or if the operational economics of staking change.

Market watchers should also avoid treating a company’s or regulator’s headline as a substitute for terms and conditions. Tokens, shares and regulated service agreements create different rights, even when they coexist in one wallet or platform. A reliable follow-up should ask which entity is responsible, what a holder can actually redeem or transfer, and whether the claimed advantages appear in live activity. Those questions are more informative than an unsupported price target or an assumption that adoption is inevitable.

title: Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Accelerate AI Expansion
summary: Bitcoin mining technology company Luxor has raised $16 million in a strategic funding round led by CMT Digital, accelerating its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure as cryptocurrency mining businesses increasingly pursue opportunities in the rapidly growing AI computing market. Lux...
content:
Bitcoin mining technology company Luxor has raised $16 million in a strategic funding round led by CMT Digital, accelerating its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure as cryptocurrency mining businesses increasingly pursue opportunities in the rapidly growing AI computing market.

Key Takeaways

  • Luxor raised $16 million in a funding round led by CMT Digital to accelerate its expansion into AI computing, hardware trading, and financial derivatives.
  • Bitcoin miners are increasingly pivoting to AI, with companies including Hut 8, Terawulf, Core Scientific, IREN, and Cipher investing heavily in AI infrastructure.
  • Luxor is taking a different approach, focusing on supplying hardware, software, and financial services to the AI industry rather than converting mining facilities into data centers.

Luxor Raises $16 Million

The Seattle-based company announced the investment Tuesday, with participation from bitcoin mining hardware manufacturers Canaan and MicroBT, along with Halo, Steelhead, and several angel investors. The financing includes both primary and secondary capital, although Luxor did not disclose the breakdown or its valuation.

The funding follows Luxor’s September launch of Luxor AI, a business division designed to bring the company’s existing expertise in energy management, computing hardware, financial derivatives, and software into the AI and high-performance computing (HPC) sectors.

Luxor said it will use the capital to expand its AI-focused cloud platform, provide working capital for its growing hardware trading business, increase its activity in computing derivatives and market-making, and hire additional engineering and business development personnel.

The company is building on its established bitcoin mining operations, which include a mining pool, specialized hardware brokerage, firmware, energy services, and financial products that allow miners to hedge fluctuations in computing revenue.

According to Luxor, its hardware brokerage has facilitated $1 billion in bitcoin mining equipment transactions, while its energy division manages more than 75 megawatts of electrical load across the ERCOT and Southwest Power Pool markets. Its AI cloud platform had processed 1.8 million workloads year-to-date as of September.

Luxor is also expanding its brokerage of graphics processing units and AI servers, tapping relationships with equipment manufacturers and suppliers to source hardware in an increasingly competitive market.

Another focus is the development of financial derivatives tied to computing capacity. Luxor already offers over-the-counter options, forwards, and other contracts linked to computing rental indexes, extending a model it previously developed for Bitcoin mining hashrate.

“Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI,” Luxor CEO and co-founder Nick Hansen said in the announcement.

Bitcoin Miners Shift Focus to AI

The investment comes as bitcoin mining companies increasingly redirect their infrastructure and capital toward AI, seeking revenue opportunities beyond the volatile economics of cryptocurrency production.

In July, Bitcoin.com News reported that Hut 8 had secured a $9.8 billion, 15-year lease for an additional 352 megawatts of AI computing capacity at its Beacon Point campus in Texas. The agreement doubled the tenant’s commitment at the site to 704 megawatts.

Meanwhile, Terawulf has undertaken an aggressive expansion into AI infrastructure. In May, the company acquired a Kentucky data center site targeting one gigawatt of high-performance computing capacity by 2030, with its AI revenue already surpassing bitcoin mining revenue during the first quarter of 2026.

Other major mining companies, including Core Scientific, IREN, and Cipher, have similarly repurposed or reduced bitcoin mining operations to accommodate AI computing customers.

The transition has not been without costs. An October analysis published by Bitcoin.com News estimated that publicly traded miners shed approximately 75 exahash per second of realized bitcoin mining capacity during the first half of 2026, representing roughly $1.5 billion in equivalent hardware investment.

Unlike operators converting large mining facilities into AI data centers, Luxor is positioning itself as a provider of the hardware, software, trading, and financial infrastructure serving both industries.

Its latest investment suggests that the convergence between bitcoin mining and AI is creating opportunities not only for companies that own data centers, but also for businesses supplying the equipment, financial products, and services supporting an expanding market for computing power.

title: Ripple and C2FO Tap XRP Ledger to Turn Payment Delays Into Seconds
summary: Ripple and C2FO are bringing invoice financing and settlement to the XRP Ledger, using Ripple’s dollar-backed stablecoin, RLUSD. The initiative targets bank transfer delays that leave suppliers waiting days for approved early payments. XRP Ledger Targets Settlement Delays Suppliers could gain faster...
content:
Ripple and C2FO are bringing invoice financing and settlement to the XRP Ledger, using Ripple’s dollar-backed stablecoin, RLUSD. The initiative targets bank transfer delays that leave suppliers waiting days for approved early payments.

Key Takeaways

  • Participating capital providers will fund instant supplier payments.
  • Existing invoice terms and due dates will remain unchanged.
  • Access will expand through a limited rollout over the coming months.

XRP Ledger Targets Settlement Delays

Suppliers could gain faster access to cash from approved invoices through an initiative announced Oct. 27 at Ripple Swell in New York. Working capital platform C2FO and blockchain infrastructure provider Ripple outlined plans to bring C2FO Instant Pay financing and settlement onto the XRP Ledger (XRPL), with Ripple USD (RLUSD) serving as the settlement asset.

Payments would settle on the XRP Ledger in three to five seconds, Ripple stated. For suppliers, C2FO said the money would reach their bank accounts within minutes after an invoice is confirmed for early payment, allowing businesses to put those funds to use sooner.

Businesses often face payment terms of 30, 60, or 90 days after delivering goods and services, tying up money needed for payroll, inventory, and orders. Even after an early payment is approved, traditional bank processing can prolong the wait.

Ragui Selwanes, C2FO’s president and chief operating officer for the Americas, noted:

“Working with Ripple and leveraging XRPL, we have built a new model for financing approved receivables that has the potential to broaden access to capital while preserving the relationships and experience our customers already trust.”

Capital Providers Fund Early Invoice Payments

Businesses will continue requesting early payments through C2FO, while participating capital providers supply the funding settled on XRPL. The arrangement preserves agreed invoice terms and due dates. Under C2FO’s existing early-payment process, suppliers select approved invoices and offer a discount to receive their money sooner.

RLUSD will provide the dollar-linked settlement asset for those transactions, extending the use of dollar-backed stablecoins for payment settlement. The ledger operates around the clock, allowing settlement outside conventional banking hours. Ripple describes transaction costs as a fraction of a cent.

Instant Pay uses the existing C2FO platform and login, with a one-time setup to connect a bank account and confirm remittance details. The product is launching through a limited rollout over the coming months, and businesses can join a waitlist as access expands. Instant Pay will be available only in the U.S. at launch.

Commercial Payments Extend RLUSD’s Use

A related RLUSD financing partnership with Arf targets licensed payment companies awaiting cross-border settlements. Arf provides short-term funding to financial institutions handling those transfers. Its Oct. 22 announcement outlined the use of RLUSD for payment-company liquidity, while C2FO focuses on approved supplier invoices.

Separately, Ripple Treasury is targeting businesses’ idle operating cash through returns on qualifying corporate RLUSD holdings. Unveiled Oct. 26, the offering covers eligible balances held overnight, over weekends, and during holidays, subject to program requirements.

Markus Infanger, senior vice president of RippleX, Ripple’s team supporting developers building on XRPL, described the commercial opportunity:

“Together with C2FO, this creates an opportunity to address billions of dollars in commercial activity and make approved receivables easier to finance.”

Strive also disclosed changes to its outstanding share count and preferred instruments. That context is crucial because a headline bitcoin total tells shareholders relatively little by itself. The programme is an authorisation, not a statement that the full amount has already been raised. Preferred dividends and funding costs create obligations that must be balanced against any future appreciation in bitcoin. Investors therefore need to look at capital structure and liquidity alongside a company’s conviction about the asset.

A rising coin balance does not eliminate dilution, financing-cost or governance concerns. The relevant comparison is not only today’s bitcoin value but also the number of coins and liabilities attributable to each share over time.

Strive’s next disclosures should reveal whether accumulation continues, how much preferred capital is actually sold and whether its bitcoin-per-share metrics improve after changes in the equity base. The difference between company shares and the underlying cryptocurrency remains substantial.

title: VanEck launches diversified ETF combining stocks, bonds and Bitcoin exposure
summary: VanEck’s new Wealth Builder ETF targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, with a permitted range of 1% to 5%, gaining exposure through a spot Bitcoin ETP.
content:
VanEck’s new Wealth Builder ETF targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, with a permitted range of 1% to 5%, gaining exposure through a spot Bitcoin ETP.

US asset manager VanEck has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund (ETF) that combines stocks, bonds and real assets with a targeted allocation to Bitcoin.

According to Tuesday’s announcement, the VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO) invests in both VanEck and third-party ETFs, with a target Bitcoin allocation of 2% and a permitted range of 1% to 5%, according to the company’s website. Bitcoin exposure comes through a spot Bitcoin ETP rather than direct holdings of the cryptocurrency.

The fund builds on VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios, previously available to financial advisers through third-party wealth management platforms. Its strategy incorporates exposure to global equities, fixed income, gold and other real assets, with allocations managed and rebalanced by VanEck.

“The traditional 60/40 portfolio was built for a different investment landscape,” said David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions. 

He said adding real assets alongside stocks and bonds could help investors navigate a wider range of economic conditions.

The launch follows VanEck’s March partnership with retirement platform Basic Capital, which made a selection of the asset manager’s digital asset exchange-traded products available through US employer-sponsored 401(k) plans. VanEck managed about $244.1 billion in assets as of Sept. 30, according to the company.

title: Intel, IBM, Oracle and IonQ latest to object to OKX-ICE tokenized stocks
summary: More than 40% of the companies initially proposed to have their stocks listed in tokenized form have asked to opt-out.
content:
More than 40% of the companies initially proposed to have their stocks listed in tokenized form have asked to opt-out.

Four companies have joined the list of those filing objections to listings on a tokenized stock exchange proposed by cryptocurrency exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

In a Monday update to its proposed OKXICE exchange, the crypto company reported that Intel, IBM, Oracle and IonQ were the most recent companies to object to having their US stocks listed in tokenized form. With the addition of the four, 26 companies have now filed to raise objections to OKXICE’s plans, including Alphabet, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs.

The proposed offering came just a few weeks after the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved temporary innovation exemptions for tokenized US stocks. Under the SEC exemption, Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) can offer limited trading for tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks. 

Many of the companies to opt out of the OKXICE plans currently have US listings on Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange. In September, Nasdaq released guidance for companies considering the innovation exemption, saying issuers should be “cautious” about participating. The exchange invested $100 million in Kraken parent Payward in September as part of its own push into tokenized assets.

OKXICE proposed 62 companies listing tokenized stocks when it filed with the SEC under the exemption, meaning about 41% of the entities have chosen not to participate as of Monday. Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of the tokenization venture, said it was a “very natural response” for some companies to object, and he expected to see more names added to the list.

title: CFTC Sues Utah, Warns Kalshi Crackdown Threatens Federal Oversight
summary: The federal government has hauled Utah into court over prediction markets, challenging a state gambling crackdown that targets Kalshi and potentially $61.2 million in trading fees. The showdown pits Washington’s derivatives regulator against one of America’s strictest gambling prohibitions. CFTC Cha...
content:
The federal government has hauled Utah into court over prediction markets, challenging a state gambling crackdown that targets Kalshi and potentially $61.2 million in trading fees. The showdown pits Washington’s derivatives regulator against one of America’s strictest gambling prohibitions.

Key Takeaways

  • The CFTC filed its 10th state lawsuit, challenging Utah’s enforcement against regulated prediction markets.
  • Utah alleges Kalshi collected up to $61.2 million in fees and caused $5.5 million in resident losses.
  • Kalshi’s earlier federal court defeat complicates the CFTC’s effort to establish exclusive jurisdiction.

CFTC Challenges Utah’s Gambling Crackdown

On Tuesday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and the United States filed suit against Utah and Attorney General Derek Brown in federal district court, seeking to prevent state authorities from enforcing gambling restrictions against federally regulated prediction markets.

The complaint, filed in the District of Utah under case number 2:26-cv-01055, argues that the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) gives the CFTC exclusive authority over event contracts traded on designated contract markets. “The United States and the CFTC bring this action to halt Defendants’ efforts to prohibit the operation of derivatives markets governed by federal law,” the complaint states.

The regulator has also filed lawsuits against nine other states over the legal boundaries of federal oversight of event-based trading contracts, including New York, Kentucky, Rhode Island, Arizona, Minnesota, Wisconsin, New Mexico, Connecticut, and Illinois.

“Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig remarked. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events.”

Selig added:

“Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.”

The agency wants a federal judge to declare Utah’s gambling and public-nuisance laws preempted when applied to covered federally regulated contracts. It also seeks preliminary and permanent injunctions preventing state officials from pursuing enforcement against regulated platforms and their business partners.

Utah Targets Kalshi Over Millions in Trading Fees

The federal challenge follows Utah’s Oct. 20 lawsuit against Kalshi, its affiliates, and two Susquehanna entities. Brown’s complaint alleges the companies operated an illegal gambling enterprise offering contracts tied to sports, elections, politics, entertainment, and other outcomes. Utah estimates Kalshi collected between $30.6 million and $61.2 million in fees from state accounts through mid-October. The state also alleges residents suffered approximately $5.5 million in trading losses.

More than 32,000 Utah residents had verified Kalshi accounts earlier in 2026. Brown accused the company of operating “an online casino in Utah and call[ing] it a prediction market.” Utah wants the activity stopped, allegedly unlawful profits surrendered and affected customers compensated. Kalshi maintains that its exchange operates under federal oversight and that individual states cannot independently prohibit its regulated contracts.

Earlier Court Defeat Complicates Federal Challenge

Interestingly, Kalshi had already lost a major round of this fight. On Aug. 4, U.S. District Judge Robert J. Shelby ruled that federal commodities law didn’t prevent Utah from enforcing its gambling prohibitions against Kalshi’s sports contracts. Kalshi appealed, but the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied its request for an injunction pending appeal on Sept. 8.

The latest CFTC complaint advances three preemption arguments: express federal authority, comprehensive federal regulation, and conflicts between state restrictions and national derivatives oversight. “The State’s actions inject uncertainty into federal derivatives markets over the scope of the Commission’s jurisdiction,” the CFTC’s complaint against Utah reads.

A ruling favoring Washington could redraw the regulatory boundaries for prediction markets nationwide. A Utah victory would strengthen states’ arguments that federally regulated contracts can still constitute prohibited gambling services. For now, the federal government is defending markets that a federal judge has already allowed Utah to restrict.

Those dates are governance milestones, not proof that every feature has already been activated. The upgrade package focuses on making smart accounts easier for large services to operate and laying groundwork for quantum-resistant signature verification and faster ledgers. It brings three technical proposals together rather than announcing a wholly new blockchain.

One proposal introduces muxed contract addresses. Traditional muxed accounts let services use a common account with customer identifiers; the new approach extends that convenience to contract-based infrastructure. For exchanges, ramps and custodians, the implication is potentially simpler handling of many customer relationships without deploying the same logic repeatedly. That is an infrastructure benefit more than a flashy wallet feature, and it will need careful implementation to preserve separation between customer records and authorisations.

Another change adds support for verifying post-quantum signatures inside smart contracts. It does not mean Stellar’s entire network instantly becomes quantum-proof. Cryptographic migration is a layered undertaking: accounts, recovery systems, software libraries and operational procedures must all be evaluated. The proposal provides a building block that developers may use, while further decisions are needed to determine when and how different security models should be adopted.

For cryptocurrency investors, the central point is to distinguish an announced milestone from an immediate change in asset value. Such work can make payment and trading applications feel more responsive, but engineers must balance latency against validator coordination and network stability. Faster ledger intervals are not automatically equivalent to instant legal settlement of offchain obligations. For enterprise users, the value will be measured by predictable performance under load as much as by an attractive headline benchmark.

Developers should watch the testnet vote, compatibility notes, upgrade documentation and the result of the planned November mainnet vote. title: Treasury's Bessent sees crypto as America's next tool for keeping the U.S. dollar on top
summary: Speaking at Ripple's conference, the U.S. Treasury Secretary said the SEC and CFTC action could help fill the gap left by the Clarity Act's failure, while curbing crypto debanking.
content:
Skip to main content

  • Crypto News

Oct 27, 2026, 4:41 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said U.S. leadership in digital assets could reinforce the dollar’s global dominance as technological strength becomes increasingly important to economic influence.
  • Bessent said Tuesday that the Treasury Department could work with the SEC and CFTC to clarify cryptocurrency rules after the failure to pass federal digital asset regulation, and establish safeguards against banks cutting off services to digital-asset businesses.
  • The Trump administration has passed the GENIUS Act, establishing federal rules for stablecoins, which Bessent argued was a way to expand global demand for U.S. dollars and Treasury debt.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said digital assets could help strengthen the U.S. dollar's global dominance as technology becomes an increasingly important source of American economic influence.

Speaking Tuesday at Ripple's Swell conference with CEO Brad Garlinghouse, Bessent argued that the power behind the world's reserve currencies during history derived from military strength, but it’s increasingly shifting toward technological leadership.

"We will keep our military umbrella, but I think more and more it's becoming a technology umbrella," Bessent said.

He pointed to the growing divide between U.S. and Chinese technology ecosystems, where countries and companies face choices over whose artificial intelligence systems and semiconductor technology to adopt. Bessent said he sees digital assets as part of that competition, with the financial infrastructure countries may choose influencing the U.S. dollar’s reach.

"I think that digital assets are going to be no different, and we are going to win in the digital asset stack, and that's gonna continue to fortify the [U.S.] dollar," he said.

His remarks offered a broader rationale for the administration of President Donald Trump’s push to bring crypto businesses onshore, framing digital assets not just as a financial market but as part of the infrastructure that could sustain U.S. economic influence. The administration has already secured passage of the GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, cryptocurrencies designed to maintain a fixed value against fiat currencies like the U.S. dollar.

Bessent argued that stablecoins could reinforce the dollar's position by expanding access to U.S. currency in countries where local currencies face inflation or sharp swings in value.

More than 90% of stablecoins are backed by U.S. dollars, he said, and their issuers often hold U.S. government securities as reserves. As adoption grows, demand for those assets could rise, creating another source of financing for the federal government.

"I think it's gonna be an important source of funding for the Treasury," Bessent said.

‘Opening new markets’

Bessent pushed back against the idea that stablecoins would merely replace dollars people already hold, arguing that they could reach new users in emerging markets who want to protect their savings from currency devaluation.

"I think we are opening up new markets all around the world," he said.

However, the White House’s broader push to regulate crypto markets suffered a setback after Congress failed to pass the Clarity Act, which would have established a federal framework for the industry.

Bessent called the failure a disappointment but said the Treasury Department could work with regulatory agencies like the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to advance oversight through agency action.

"At Treasury, we have a lot of convening powers," he said, describing the SEC and CFTC as “great partners” in forming a regulatory framework that could serve as a model for other countries.

The agencies' regulatory efforts could provide more clarity for crypto firms, though rules adopted by regulators would lack the permanence of legislation.

Bessent also addressed the industry's concerns about debanking, a term used to describe financial institutions cutting off services to crypto businesses, sometimes allegedly under regulatory pressure.

He said the Clarity Act would have helped prevent a return to such practices but argued that regulatory safeguards could still offer protection.

"I think we can set up regulatory best practices, guardrails that will prevent that from happening again," Bessent said.

title: Quantum fears already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says
summary: Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Muneeb Ali warned that uncertainty over Bitcoin’s quantum security could deter institutional investors.
content:
Concerns about quantum computing are slowing institutional investment in Bitcoin, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network needs a credible roadmap for security upgrades to restore investor confidence.

“There is already a ceiling on the growth of Bitcoin because of quantum fears,” Ali said during an interview on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast. He argued that uncertainty could lead risk-averse institutional investors to delay large Bitcoin purchases until developers establish a credible path toward quantum-resistant security.

Stacks is a Bitcoin layer-2 network designed to bring smart contracts and decentralized applications to Bitcoin. Ali co-founded the project, which uses Bitcoin as its underlying settlement layer.

Chain Reaction Podcast. Source: Cointelegraph

Ali warned that Bitcoin could enter a riskier period if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum-resistant security by 2028. He said upgrades typically take years to implement, with additional time needed for users to move their holdings to new addresses.

Ali pointed to 2030 as a target for transitioning to quantum-resistant security, citing guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). He suggested advances in artificial intelligence could accelerate the development of quantum computers, potentially bringing that timeline forward to 2029.

Ali acknowledged that some Bitcoin proponents believe the quantum computing threat remains distant and concerns are overblown. He argued, however, that disagreements over the urgency of the threat could themselves undermine investor confidence, particularly without a credible upgrade roadmap.

Related: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet

Bitcoin’s quantum security debate

Despite his concerns, Ali said a sufficiently powerful quantum computer would more likely emerge from a major research laboratory than an unknown attacker. He suggested companies such as Google or Microsoft would have little incentive to use the technology to steal Bitcoin, given the potential legal consequences.

Ali also said a quantum security threat to Bitcoin would affect the broader cryptocurrency industry, even projects developing their own protections. “If Bitcoin gets hit, everyone gets hit downstream as well,” he said.

Meanwhile, developers are exploring ways to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks. In September, StarkWare reported that researchers had reduced the estimated computing cost of preparing an experimental quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction by 79%, following a weeklong optimization challenge.

The approach requires no changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules, but the latest cost reductions have been demonstrated only in benchmark tests. StarkWare has described the technology as a last-resort measure and continues to advocate for a protocol-level upgrade as a longer-term solution.
