title: Crypto Midterm Election Spending Reaches $176 Million as Industry Builds for the Next Congress
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Crypto Midterm Election Spending Reaches $176 Million as Industry Builds for the Next Congress
The crypto industry has spent about $176 million on more than 100 midterm races to build a bipartisan bloc in Congress that can protect its interests after Trump leaves office.
This post ...
content:
The crypto industry has spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this cycle, according to a Reuters review of campaign spending. The money is part of a plan to build a bipartisan coalition in Congress that can protect the sector after President Donald Trump leaves office.

Fairshake, the industry’s largest super PAC, leads the effort. The group spent $196 million in the 2024 cycle and is directing strategy again. Through October 20, Fairshake and its affiliate PACs had spent about $150.8 million this year, while other crypto groups spent around $25 million. Fairshake said 53 of the 58 candidates it backed in primaries or special elections won, and those candidates will be on the November 3 ballot, per Reuters. 

Super PACs can raise and spend unlimited sums but cannot coordinate with campaigns. Fairshake’s ads run through affiliates with names such as “Defend American Jobs” and “Protect Progress,” and they often focus on taxes and immigration rather than crypto. Voters have little way of knowing who pays for them. 

The watchdog group Public Citizen said crypto was the largest corporate spender in federal races in 2026. Crypto firms led corporate political spending at that point, citing the same watchdog’s analysis.

Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz are the primary financiers. Industry strategists and campaign staff said the money is a calling card meant to build relationships with elected officials. 

Crypto’s long game in Congress

Colin McLaren, head of government relations at the Solana Policy Institute, which has given $4.9 million to the midterms, called it “an investment in the future,” per Reuters.

The approach reflects a sharp change. In 2018, lawmakers could not secure a room in the House or Senate office buildings for the first bipartisan crypto roundtable, so they met at the Library of Congress. Then, under the Biden administration, the Securities and Exchange Commission levied more than $6 billion in penalties across 98 cases, according to a Georgetown University Law study. 

Executives concluded they needed political force. Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad helped launch Stand With Crypto and Fairshake in 2023. The number of lawmakers rated “A” by Stand With Crypto rose to 332 from 96 when the group launched.

Legislation followed. The GENIUS Act, enacted in 2025 with broad bipartisan support, created the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins. The industry’s next goal, the Clarity Act, would place oversight under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. That bill stalled this session. Senate Democrats blocked it from reaching a final vote over an ethics provision that would have forced the Trump family to sell its crypto holdings. 

Fairshake helped defeat Sherrod Brown, who chaired the Senate Banking Committee, in 2024, and the industry has since spent more than $68 million on his rematch against Republican Jon Husted, according to AdImpact. 

Fairshake’s ads against Brown do not mention crypto, and Brown’s campaign manager, Patrick Eisenhauer, said “the special interests are panicking.” In Illinois, Fairshake spent over $10.1 million attacking Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton and $2.5 million against state Representative La Shawn Ford, per Reuters, yet both are expected to win on November 3. 

Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss each gave about $13 million this cycle, most of it to MAGA Inc.

What voters think

Public attitudes are mixed. A September survey seen by Bitcoin Magazine of 1,545 U.S. adults by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund found that 22% have owned or used crypto, up from 18% in 2025. Only 19% believe the U.S. financial system is secure. 

The survey also found 35% say it is important for candidates to support building the next generation of financial technology in the United States. Only 13% said the same when the question named blockchain, crypto or DeFi. The DeFi Education Fund is a digital asset advocacy group, so its framing reflects that perspective. 

Stand With Crypto’s leadership has argued that the crypto vote will decide the midterms.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Nasdaq-100 comes onchain as Janus Henderson and Centrifuge launch first licensed fund
summary: The $500 billion asset manager is launching an issuer-sponsored fund on Stellar, taking a different approach from third-party stock tokens.
content:
Oct 27, 2026, 10:21 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Janus Henderson and Centrifuge launched JQQQ, an issuer-sponsored onchain fund on the Stellar blockchain that tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index.
  • The fund differs from third-party stock tokens because Janus Henderson issues and manages it, Centrifuge provides its blockchain infrastructure and Nasdaq licenses the index.
  • The launch expands Wall Street’s tokenization push into stock-market products and brings Janus Henderson’s onchain investment platform to more than $1 billion in assets.

Janus Henderson, a London-based asset manager overseeing roughly $500 billion, is bringing one of Wall Street’s best-known stock indexes onto blockchain rails through an issuer-sponsored fund. The launch comes amid an escalating debate over who gets to tokenize traditional securities.

The firm teamed up with tokenization platform Centrifuge to launch JQQQ, a fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 Index, home to tech giants including Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft. The fund is issued on the Stellar XLM$0.1853 blockchain, the companies said Tuesday.

JQQQ follows the introduction of a similar onchain index fund product last year, the Janus Henderson Anemoy S&P 500 Fund (SPXA), which was the first tokenized index fund licensed by the S&P Dow Jones Indices.

Janus Henderson said its onchain investment platform now includes more than $1 billion across Treasuries, structured credit and equities.

The launch marks another step in Wall Street’s push to bring traditional investments onchain, expanding beyond U.S. Treasuries, money market funds and private credit into stock-market products. It also highlights a growing divide between funds issued onchain by their managers and third-party tokens created without the underlying companies’ involvement.

Issuer-backed versus third-party tokens

JQQQ follows the issuer-sponsored model. Janus Henderson issues and manages the fund, Centrifuge provides the blockchain infrastructure and Nasdaq licenses the index to track.

That differs from third-party stock tokens, which may be backed by shares held in custody or structured as separate instruments tracking stock prices. Investors in those products don't necessarily own the underlying shares or receive shareholder rights.

The distinction has become central in the debate around tokenization efforts. Most recently, 22 companies objected to plans for blockchain-based trading of their shares on the OKX-ICE venue, adding to a debate over whether issuers should have a say when their stocks are tokenized.

“As investors explore new ways to access markets through digital infrastructure, demand continues to grow for exposure to established, transparent benchmarks,” said Sean Wasserman, head of index product management at Nasdaq.

The fund also shows how tokenization is moving beyond digital versions of existing investments toward products built to operate on blockchains from the start.

Such funds could eventually allow investors to use their holdings as collateral for loans or move them between blockchain-based financial applications, subject to regulatory requirements and platform support.

"Tokenization becomes much more powerful when the assets investors want to own can also become building blocks for an onchain financial system," said Anil Sood, chief strategy and growth officer at Centrifuge.

title: CF Benchmarks brings Wall Street pricing infrastructure onchain, including data used by BlackRock
summary: The new service could help developers build blockchain-based index funds, tokenized portfolios and derivatives using established financial benchmarks.
content:
Oct 27, 2026, 10:00 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • CF Benchmarks is making the pricing indices used by BlackRock and CME Group available to blockchain-based financial applications.
  • The new service could help developers build onchain index funds, tokenized portfolios and derivatives using established market benchmarks.
  • Kraken parent Payward plans to use the service for a U.S. perpetual futures offering powered by Hyperliquid, pending regulatory approval.

CF Benchmarks, whose pricing indices underpin BlackRock's bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) and CME Group's crypto futures, is bringing its market data to blockchain networks as more financial firms look to offer traditional investment products through decentralized finance (DeFi).

The company, which is owned by Kraken parent Payward, has introduced CFB Oracle, a service that gives blockchain applications access to its benchmarks for cryptocurrencies, stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies.

The idea is to make the same pricing infrastructure used by major financial institutions available to developers building investment products on blockchains.

For example, a blockchain-based fund holding tokenized stocks would need reliable prices to calculate the value of its portfolio. A lending platform accepting tokenized bonds as collateral would need that data to determine how much users can borrow and when positions should be liquidated.

CF Benchmarks already provides this type of pricing data to traditional financial markets. Its indices are used by products representing more than $120 billion in assets, according to the company.

With CFB Oracle, developers can use those benchmarks to build products such as onchain index funds, tokenized portfolios and derivatives without having to develop their own pricing systems. The service is available on Ethereum ETH$2,490.55, HyperEVM and Robinhood Chain, with plans to support other compatible networks.

CF Benchmarks says the data is digitally signed, allowing applications to check that prices came from the company and haven't been altered. It also publishes each index at the same frequency for all customers, rather than charging for faster access.

The service has a planned use within Payward. The Kraken parent intends to use CFB Oracle to supply pricing data for an upcoming U.S. perpetual futures offering powered by Hyperliquid (HYPE). That product is still awaiting regulatory approval.

The launch puts CF Benchmarks in competition with oracle providers such as Chainlink LINK$12.64 and Pyth, which already supply market data to decentralized trading and lending platforms.

CFB Oracle won't issue funds or handle trades itself. Its role is to supply the reference prices those products need to operate.

title: Mirae Asset Securities and Grvt Collaborate on Tokenised Funding Note Issuance
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 27th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 27th October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 27th, 2026, Chainwire

The collaboration begins with Grvt’s subscription to Mirae Asset Securities’ tokenised funding notes, with potential future tokenised products (e.g., tokenised Treasuries, corporate bonds and ETFs) to be explored, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

Mirae Asset Securities (HK) Limited, the Hong Kong subsidiary of Korea’s leading securities firm, has arranged an issuance of tokenised funding notes under its affiliate’s structured notes programme, to which Grvt has subscribed. Grvt intends to use the resulting exposure in connection with Grvt Earn, subject to applicable requirements. 

Grvt Earn is offered and operated independently by Grvt and is available only to eligible users in permitted jurisdictions. Grvt has subscribed for the notes. Any use of the resulting exposure in connection with Grvt Earn is independently determined and managed by Grvt.

From Tokenised Funding Notes to Tokenised ETFs

Tokenised funding notes are the starting point. The two firms will next explore additional tokenised products (including Treasuries and ETFs) on a non-committed and exploratory basis, subject to applicable regulatory approvals and product/compliance clearance.

Mirae Asset Financial Group oversees more than US$1 trillion in client assets worldwide as of Sep 2026. The parties intend to explore opportunities involving selected tokenised products, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

The transaction represents an initial collaboration between the two firms. The parties may explore further opportunities involving tokenised products, subject to applicable legal and regulatory requirements and their respective internal approvals.

Mirae Asset Securities’ Digital Asset Expansion

Mirae Asset Securities has moved quickly to connect traditional finance and digital assets in 2026. In January, it became the first Korean securities firm to issue digital bonds in Hong Kong. In April, Mirae Asset Securities (HK) Limited became the first Korean-owned brokerage to receive the Securities and Futures Commission (“SFC”) approval to offer digital asset trading to retail investors. In July, it launched MAPS in Hong Kong, a single app for traditional and digital assets with products allowed by the SFC. 

“When Korea’s leading securities firm explores opportunities in tokenised assets, collaboration with market participants plays an important role. Grvt’s subscription to Mirae Asset Securities’ tokenised funding notes marks an initial step in this collaboration. Together, we intend to explore opportunities involving tokenised Treasuries, corporate bonds and, over time, ETFs for eligible investors in permitted jurisdictions, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.” Hong Yea, Co-founder and CEO, Grvt 

“We see tokenisation as an important area of development for capital markets. Grvt’s subscription to this tokenised funding note issuance represents an opportunity to explore the use of tokenised securities in new market structures. We look forward to exploring further opportunities.”

“This issuance marks a step forward in our digital asset strategy, bringing our structured product capabilities into tokenised markets. We look forward to exploring further opportunities with Grvt, subject to applicable regulatory requirements and internal approvals.”  Kelly Sohn, Head of Digital Assets, Mirae Asset Securities (HK) Limited

About Grvt 

Grvt is an onchain platform, live since 2024. Users trade, invest, and earn from a single account that only their own key can move. title: PrimeXBT Brings Tesla, SpaceX, NVIDIA and More to Crypto Futures with New Tokenised Stocks
summary: Castries, Saint Lucia, 27th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Castries, Saint Lucia, 27th October 2026, Chainwire

Castries, Saint Lucia, October 27th, 2026, Chainwire

PrimeXBT, a global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider, has announced a major expansion of its offering, introducing Tokenised Stocks, a new category of Crypto Futures available on its native PXTrader 2.0 platform. The launch gives crypto traders access to price movements linked to some of the world’s most prominent companies, bringing opportunities from traditional equity markets into the crypto trading environment.

The new category includes seven USDT-denominated Crypto Futures linked to SpaceX (SPCX/USDT), NVIDIA (NVDA/USDT), Tesla (TSLA/USDT), Circle (CRCL/USDT), Apple (AAPL/USDT), Alphabet (GOOGL/USDT) and Robinhood (HOOD/USDT). Traders can take long or short positions and respond to market developments around the clock, including outside traditional stock exchange hours. The contracts provide exposure to company-linked price movements without ownership of the underlying shares.

“Big Tech remains at the centre of market attention, with AI investment, corporate earnings and growth expectations driving sentiment across global equities. Earnings season in particular can bring significant price movements, as investors reassess company performance and future prospects,” commented Jonatan Randin, Senior Market Analyst at PrimeXBT. “With tokenised stocks, we’re opening up new opportunities to crypto traders, allowing them to participate in major equity market trends through a familiar crypto trading environment.”

Alongside Tokenised Stocks, PrimeXBT has added Lighter (LIT/USDT), Monad (MON/USDT), Venice Token (VVV/USDT), Canton (CC/USDT), Stable (STABLE/USDT), JUST (JST/USDT) and Midnight (NIGHT/USDT) to its PXTrader 2.0 lineup of over 170 Crypto Futures, further strengthening the depth and diversity of its offering across DeFi, AI, Gaming, Payments, Layer 1 and 2 networks, blockchain infrastructure, NFTs, Meme coins and the Metaverse. The broker has also introduced new Crypto CFDs on Monero (XMR/USD), Hyperliquid (HYPE/USD) and Zcash (ZEC/USD) on PXTrader 2.0, with corresponding USDT-quoted instruments available on MetaTrader 5.

PrimeXBT has also expanded its blockchain network support with the addition of Arbitrum, Optimism and Base, joining existing networks including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB Smart Chain and Solana. Additionally, the broker has added Tether Gold (XAUT), a tokenized gold asset, to its internal Exchange, expanding its offering of over 50 cryptocurrencies and digital assets.

The expanded offering is supported by flexible crypto funding and crypto-denominated accounts in USDT, USDC, BTC and ETH, allowing clients to trade without converting their holdings into fiat. PrimeXBT offers competitive Crypto Futures fees of 0.01% for makers and 0.045% for takers, with further discounts through its volume-based VIP program. New clients automatically receive VIP 4 status for their first 14 days, reducing Crypto Futures taker fees by 33%, while high-volume traders can unlock fees as low as 0.015% and Bitcoin CFD spreads from $19 at the highest VIP tier.

The launch reflects the growing convergence of crypto and traditional financial markets, bringing a wider range of global market trends into the crypto trading environment. From artificial intelligence and electric vehicles to space technology and digital finance, PrimeXBT continues to broaden trading opportunities beyond digital assets, reinforcing its position as an innovative multi-asset broker connecting markets through one trading ecosystem.

To learn more about the Crypto Futures offering, users can visit PrimeXBT’s website.

About PrimeXBT

PrimeXBT is a global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider trusted by traders in more than 150 countries. The platform bridges traditional and digital markets within one integrated environment, redefining versatility and innovation in online trading. Clients can access Forex, CFDs on indices, commodities, shares, crypto, and Crypto Futures, as well as buy, store and exchange cryptocurrencies. This unified experience extends across both the native PXTrader 2.0 platform and MetaTrader 5, supported by advanced risk-management tools and a wide range of funding options in crypto, fiat and local payment methods. Since 2018, PrimeXBT has focused on empowering traders through broad multi-asset access, fair and transparent conditions, professional-grade technology and dedicated human support. By combining expertise, trust and a client-first approach, PrimeXBT sets a benchmark of excellence in the financial industry and provides traders with the tools they need to trade, grow and succeed with confidence.

title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to 60,000 Employees as AI Spending Surges Toward $190 Billion
summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees—about 27% of its global workforce—as it prepares to spend up to $190 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026.
content:
Skip to content

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees—about 27% of its global workforce—as it prepares to spend up to $190 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026.

The program targets eligible workers in the US, Canada, the UK, and India, highlighting Microsoft’s effort to balance soaring AI investment with tighter cost control.

Microsoft Buyout Program Targets 60,000 Employees

The voluntary exit offer covers eligible employees at level 70 and below, including some vice president-level positions. Participating divisions include Copilot, finance, human resources, and Xbox, while certain marketing, commercial, and security teams are excluded, according to media reports.

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees, or a quarter of its global workforce, to reduce costs and refocus on AI. Source: Bloomberg via X

Microsoft Chief People Officer Amy Coleman described the program as a way to give employees more flexibility while helping the company adapt to changing business needs.

“The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it,” Coleman wrote in an internal memo, adding that the company aims to create opportunities for employees to grow and contribute.

Eligible employees are expected to make their decisions by early December, with departures scheduled for December 31, 2026. The company has not said how many employees it expects to accept the offer.

Microsoft AI Spending Reaches Up to $190 Billion

Microsoft’s buyout initiative coincides with plans to spend approximately $175 billion to $190 billion on capital investments in 2026, supporting data centers, specialized AI hardware, cooling systems, and energy infrastructure.

Microsoft is projected to spend nearly $190 billion on AI expansion in 2026, primarily to build data centers. Source: @arnaudmercier via X

The investment underpins Microsoft’s efforts to expand Azure cloud computing and integrate AI tools into products such as Microsoft 365 Copilot. Azure also provides computing capacity for AI developers, including the company’s partner OpenAI.

However, building AI infrastructure requires substantial upfront investment and ongoing operating expenses. Investors are increasingly focused on whether revenue from AI services can justify these costs.

The buyout program could help Microsoft manage payroll expenses as infrastructure spending rises. However, the company has not disclosed the expected savings or linked the program to a specific AI investment budget.

Microsoft Builds on Earlier Workforce Reductions

The new initiative follows the company’s voluntary early retirement program earlier in 2026, which was offered to approximately 8,750 U.S. employees. Around 30% of eligible workers accepted that offer, according to the company.

Microsoft’s employee growth vs. revenue growth chart. Source: *Walter Bloomberg via X

The company also cut approximately 4,800 jobs three months later. Those reductions were separate from the latest voluntary program.

The company reported approximately 223,000 full-time employees worldwide at the end of June. The latest offer gives eligible workers another departure option as the company adjusts staffing across selected business units.

Although the restructuring coincides with growing AI investment, Microsoft has not said that artificial intelligence is directly replacing every position covered by the program.

Big Tech Companies Redirect Spending Toward AI

Microsoft’s move reflects a broader technology-sector trend. Companies are reducing operating costs while directing more capital toward AI infrastructure and computing capacity.

Oracle has announced significant workforce reductions as it expands its cloud operations. Amazon and Meta have also cut corporate positions amid efforts to manage expenses and increase AI investment.

Microsoft is cutting labor costs while prioritizing AI infrastructure spending, reflecting how AI investment is reshaping Big Tech employment. Source: @DeItaone via X

Employment data from Challenger, Gray & Christmas cited in recent reports indicates that technology accounted for roughly 30% of announced job cuts in 2026.

Companies are taking different approaches, including compulsory layoffs, voluntary departures, and internal reorganizations. These measures can reduce expenses, but businesses must also retain the talent needed to develop products and serve customers.

For Microsoft, the challenge is to balance its established software operations with the infrastructure and expertise required to compete in AI.

Azure Growth and AI Returns Remain in Focus

Microsoft’s AI strategy depends heavily on Azure cloud growth and the adoption of Copilot across enterprise software. These services offer opportunities for recurring revenue, but their profitability must be weighed against the cost of computing infrastructure and product development.

Investors are watching how quickly AI demand translates into sustainable revenue and whether infrastructure spending will deliver adequate returns.

The company’s quarterly earnings report, scheduled for October 28, is expected to provide further insight into cloud performance, AI demand, and capital spending.

The voluntary buyout program offers Microsoft another way to adjust its workforce without relying exclusively on compulsory layoffs. Its financial impact will depend on employee participation, the resulting cost savings, and the growth of its AI and cloud businesses.

title: Trading Places: What 275 Senior Moves Reveal about the Industry
summary: With the summer lull well behind us and the fourth-quarter sprint underway, we decided to track where the industry's top talent has moved in the meantime. Over a critical four-month window spanning June through September, Finance Magnates logged 275 moves across brokers, crypto exchanges and prop fi...
content:
2026-10-27T13:00:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 27/10/2026 | 11:00 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • Finance Magnates logged the talent flow from June to September to uncover how retail brokers, crypto exchanges and prop firms are recalibrating their leadership teams across key global markets.
  • The GCC continues to be a pole of attraction, AI talent is in high demand, and the blended prop-and-broker landscape continues to evolve.

With the summer lull well behind us and the fourth-quarter sprint underway, we decided to track where the industry's top talent has moved in the meantime. Over a critical four-month window spanning June through September, Finance Magnates logged 275 moves across brokers, crypto exchanges and prop firms.

Our data focuses on high-level appointments – managerial posts, regional directors and the C-suite – and promotions, as well as executives splintering off to create their own ventures.

Some findings confirm prevailing market narratives, such as the blurring of lines between CFDs, funded accounts and crypto, or Dubai’s cemented status as an executive hotbed.

Interesting outliers, though, emerge.

While this pool does not represent the full gamut of Q3 mobility, it is a leading indicator of where the chips will fall this winter.

The AI Race is Getting Hot

Perhaps the most telling shift is who companies are hiring. While sales and marketing naturally continue to dominate, tech leaders represent a noticeable shift, particularly CTOs and CISOs.

For most, AI is a key part of the roadmap.

NinjaTrader underscored this by creating a Chief Innovation and AI Officer role, filled internally by Chief Product Officer Brian Weis.

The first half of 2026 has been a testbed for agentic trading, with a host of brokers, alongside the two most prominent platform providers – MetaQuotes and Spotware – integrating models like ChatGPT and Claude.

The last quarter of the year will most likely see this trend continue, with AI-driven chat support layered on top.

The Great Convergence

The walls separating traditional CFDs, prop trading, prediction markets, and crypto are becoming thinner and thinner.

The prop and retail brokerage models, in particular, are seeing the most convergence. Rather than building from scratch, brokers are buying prop executives and vice versa to launch their respective units. Senior figures are now moving fluidly between the two models, which are becoming a single career ladder.

Related: Prop Trading Slips Down Paris’ Agenda as the US Steps Up

Dues X Capital took this to its logical extreme, installing former IG Group and Capital.com executive Tim Plummer as CEO of both its prop firm (FunderPro) and its offshore CFD broker (NextTrade), treating the models as a single operational stack.

Meanwhile, crypto exchanges continue to hire directly out of the CFD talent pool to satisfy stringent onshore regulators, signaling that the transition away from the crypto native executive is reaching its inflection point.

Cyprus is ground zero for this convergence.

In a single week in August, Revolut hired the former CEO of Trading.com (Georgios Vasiliou) to run its MiCA-licensed crypto unit, Crypto.com hired BDSwiss’s former CCO/AMLCO (Stelios Moyseos) to head its MiFID operations, and as previously mentioned, Kraken onboarded a regtech specialist ( Andreas Roussos) for its own MiFID unit.

It appears the industry is discovering what traditional banking has long understood: robust compliance is a prerequisite for commercial continuity.

It’s also worth pointing out that in the race to decouple from crypto volatility – recently, Bidget CEO named Robinhood a direct competitor – exchanges are hunting talent to build out tokenization and prediction markets.

The Pull of the Desert

Geographically, the Middle East continues to drain talent from legacy hubs. Brokers and exchanges in Dubai and Abu Dhabi aggressively staff up to secure onshore licensing under the UAE’s Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA) and Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA).

A recent FinTop recruitment survey highlights that compliance chiefs in Dubai can earn up to $425,000 annually. Driven by regulatory licensing mandates, these earnings surpass the salary caps for both Chief Technology Officers and chief revenue officers.

Among the most notable moves is Crypto.com hiring Maria Allott from rival firm OKX. In her new role, she will lead prediction markets as a distinct product division in Dubai, in addition to overseeing tokenization initiatives. With ESMA classifying prediction markets as binary options of yesteryear, Dubai is a likely draw for those seeking to expand their global footprint.

It is also worth mentioning Epic Markets, a heavily capitalized newcomer to the CFD landscape. Founded by New York-based former Citadel executives Bryan Seegers and Kevin Kimmel, the venture secured an eye-catching $10 million pre-seed round in July from sole investor Karatage. Epic Markets appears to aim for an operational footprint in both the US and the UAE.

Still, Europe retains its gravitational pull, driven primarily by the need to manage regulatory risk across the FCA, CySEC, BaFin, and the EU's MiCA framework.

Conversely, APAC is seeing a localized shift, with some executives leaving the CFD space for domestic startups or launching their own Introducing Broker businesses.

This flurry of senior movements underscores the fundamental structural changes the entire trading ecosystem is undergoing. Firms poured immense capital into poaching top talent in Dubai, bringing in AI-ready CTOs and aggressively expanding into new product lines, specifically tokenization and prediction markets. As for those who spent the third quarter simply enjoying the sunshine, they may find the winter winds rather bruising.

title: Quant (QNT) Price Prediction: Falling Wedge Breakout Signals Potential 40% Rally Beyond $300
summary: Quant (QNT) rebounded above $200 in late October trading, recovering from a sharp pullback and bringing higher price targets back into focus.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: QNT

Quant (QNT) rebounded above $200 in late October trading, recovering from a sharp pullback and bringing higher price targets back into focus.

Quant’s recent price recovery has coincided with renewed buying activity and growing attention to Quant Network’s role in institutional tokenized deposit infrastructure.

Market data recorded QNT near $216 on October 26, following a 13.63% daily gain, after the asset had fallen toward $174–$178 during the previous sessions. The rebound has strengthened the short-term technical picture, although resistance above current levels could determine whether the recovery develops into a broader rally.

QNT Price Prediction: Key Technical Levels to Watch

Quant’s daily chart presents a cautiously constructive outlook. The token is trading above its 50-day and 100-day moving averages, which remain below the current price and indicate that the broader recovery structure is intact. However, shorter-term momentum indicators suggest that buyers have not yet established a decisive upward trend.

Quant (QNT) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has remained around neutral territory, while the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) has shown mixed momentum. These readings suggest that QNT has room to advance without entering clearly overbought territory, but they do not independently confirm another sustained rally.

The $198–$203 region is an immediate area to monitor as QNT attempts to establish support above $200. A sustained move through the $211–$216 resistance zone would provide a stronger indication that buyers are regaining control. Beyond that level, the next potential resistance areas sit around $225–$230, followed by the $250–$263 region.

On the downside, $182–$190 represents an important support zone. A breakdown below $182 could expose the mid-$170s, where QNT recently attracted buying interest. Further weakness could bring the lower end of its broader trading range into view.

These levels remain conditional rather than guaranteed price destinations. Traders will need to assess whether trading volume and follow-through buying support any move beyond resistance.

QNT Breaks Falling Wedge, Putting $300 in Focus

An eight-hour chart analysis published by DigitalChartist on TradingView identified a breakout above a falling wedge resistance line, accompanied by increased trading volume. The pattern can signal a potential bullish reversal, although confirmation depends on whether the price maintains the breakout.

QNT has broken above the falling wedge resistance, with a confirmed breakout potentially targeting $238.28, $253.48, $275.11, and $302.67. Source: DigitalChartist on TradingView

QNT is now facing resistance around the Ichimoku cloud, which could limit further gains in the near term. A retest of the broken wedge boundary would not necessarily invalidate the bullish setup, provided the former resistance area holds as support.

DigitalChartist outlined potential upside targets at $238.28, $253.48, $275.11, and $302.67. These projections place the $300 level within the pattern’s potential recovery range, but QNT would first need to overcome several intermediate resistance zones.

The analyst’s targets should be treated as technical scenarios rather than forecasts with guaranteed outcomes. A rejection at the Ichimoku cloud or a return below the wedge breakout could weaken the setup and extend the current consolidation.

The TradingView video highlights QNT’s descending trendline, Fibonacci levels, and projected recovery toward the $373 swing high and beyond. Source: @gandreou007 via X

Another technical perspective came from crypto analyst @gandreou007, who shared a weekly chart analysis on October 25. The analyst identified the $178.12 Fibonacci retracement level, corresponding to the 0.618 ratio, alongside support near $173. The analysis suggested that defending this region could support a bullish recovery.

The analyst also identified $130–$136 as a deeper support area if the lower levels failed. On the upside, the analysis pointed to $215 as an important recovery threshold, with the $350–$360 region representing a broader resistance barrier before a potential move toward $500.

Together, the chart analyses identify several hurdles between QNT’s recent recovery and a move beyond $300. The immediate test remains whether the token can sustain its position above $200 and break through the $211–$216 resistance zone.

Quant’s Institutional Adoption Adds to Market Interest

Beyond technical indicators, Quant’s involvement in institutional payment infrastructure provides another development for investors to monitor.

On September 24, The Clearing House announced that it had selected Quant to support its On-Chain Money Initiative, a proposed network designed to facilitate the clearing and settlement of tokenized bank deposits. Quant’s technology will provide interoperability, orchestration, and transaction management while connecting the network to existing payment systems, including RTP and CHIPS.

Quant Network was selected by The Clearing House in September 2026 to support a tokenized deposit network targeting launch in H1 2027, integrating with existing payment systems RTP and CHIPS. Source: @BSCNews via X

The network is expected to become available to participating financial institutions in the first half of 2027. Its intended applications include corporate treasury management, liquidity operations, and digital settlement.

Tokenized deposits are digital representations of bank deposits rather than conventional payment stablecoins. They can enable programmable transactions while remaining linked to deposits held within the banking system. Quant’s role in connecting these transactions with existing financial infrastructure could support demand for its technology if institutional adoption expands.

The development also comes amid changes to the US digital asset regulatory framework. On October 21, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency finalized rules implementing the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuers and certain related activities under its jurisdiction. The rules are scheduled to take effect on January 18, 2027.

Although this regulatory development provides broader context for institutional digital asset activity, it does not establish a direct catalyst for QNT’s price. The relationship between Quant’s enterprise business, adoption of its technology, and demand for the QNT token should be assessed separately.

QNT Price Outlook: Can Quant Sustain a Rally Beyond $300?

Quant’s recovery above $200 has improved its near-term technical position, while the falling wedge breakout has introduced potential upside targets extending toward $300. Nevertheless, resistance levels and mixed momentum indicators suggest that further confirmation is needed before a sustained rally can be established.

A decisive move above $211–$216 could strengthen the bullish case and bring $225–$230 into focus. If buying pressure continues, the $250–$263 area could become the next test before QNT approaches the $275–$303 range identified in the eight-hour chart analysis.

Conversely, failure to maintain support between $182 and $190 could undermine the recovery and expose the mid-$170s. A deeper decline would weaken the immediate bullish structure and shift attention toward lower support levels.

Quant’s institutional partnerships provide a longer-term development to watch, particularly as tokenized deposit infrastructure moves toward deployment. However, adoption timelines, market conditions, and actual demand for QNT remain important uncertainties.

For now, the key question is whether QNT can convert its rebound above $200 into a sustained breakout. A confirmed move through resistance would improve the technical outlook, while a failure to hold support would suggest that the latest recovery may remain part of a broader consolidation.

title: Chainlink Targets $700B Custody Market With CustodySync and Anchorage DeFi Access
summary:
Key Takeaways: Chainlink introduced CustodySync, a new solution that connects loan markets in DeFi and qualified custody. The launch partner is Anchorage Digital Bank, with institutional clients able to borrow
The post Chainlink Targets $700B Custody Market With CustodySync and Anchorage DeFi Access...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Chainlink introduced CustodySync, a new solution that connects loan markets in DeFi and qualified custody.
  • The launch partner is Anchorage Digital Bank, with institutional clients able to borrow collateral that stays in Anchorage.
  • According to Chainlink, there are approximately $700 billion of digital assets caged in custodians and could be directed toward onchain lending.

Chainlink is enabling an alternative path for institutional funds to join the DeFi space without moving assets out of regulated custody.

The company introduced CustodySync with Anchorage Digital Bank as its first partner, targeting institutions that want DeFi liquidity but still need qualified custody, internal controls and strict risk management.

  • Chainlink CustodySync Connects $700B in Custodied Crypto to DeFi
  • Collateral Stays in Custody While Loans Move Onchain
    • Chainlink Uses CRE, Proof of Reserve and Data Feeds in One Stack

Chainlink CustodySync Connects $700B in Custodied Crypto to DeFi

Traditional custody markets account for about $250 trillion, according to Chainlink, compared to an estimated $700 billion worth of digital assets in custody. Meanwhile, DeFi lending markets have over $30 billion in active locked-up loans and over $80 billion in deposits.

Its purpose is to harmonize those two systems, CustodySync. An institution does not have to move the assets to the lending protocol, it can hold them with a qualified custodian and then put them to use onchain to borrow.

Anchorage Digital Bank serves as the official launch partner and uses its Atlas Collateral Management infrastructure to coordinate collateral, margin monitoring and liquidation processes.

Read More: SEC Proposes New Crypto Custody Rules to Unlock Multi-Trillion Dollar Market Access

Collateral Stays in Custody While Loans Move Onchain

The balance of collateral remains in the control of the custodian with the structure. Chainlink Proof of Reserve publishes the custody balances onchain, and a transfer restricted receipt token is the collateral in the lending market. The token mirrors the amount held in custody but does not create an independent claim outside the lending arrangement.

The borrowed assets then flow directly from the DeFi market to the institutional borrower.

Chainlink Data Feeds would feed prices to the lending protocol, while Data Streams would pass the prices up to the custodian’s off-chain systems. That helps to minimize the potential for the two parties to do inconsistent liquidations or for them to determine different loan-to-value ratios.

Chainlink Uses CRE, Proof of Reserve and Data Feeds in One Stack

CustodySync combines several Chainlink products into a single institutional workflow.

The Chainlink Runtime Environment is responsible for managing interactions between the custody systems and the onchain markets. Proof of Reserve is used to complete balance checks on the system and Data Feeds and Data Streams help to ensure the values of the collaterals are consistent across both environments.

When a position exceeds its limits, the appointed collateral agent ensures the process of a sale is run. During liquidation, CustodySync makes sure the lending position doesn’t lose synchronization by onboarding the proceeds onchain before final settlement.

Anchorage Digital Bank is the first qualified custodian to have implemented CustodySync. They said the bank’s already had collateral management working on its Atlas instruments for institutional loans, monitoring, as well as margin call and margin liquidation workflows.

title: Brad Garlinghouse Announces Final OCC Approval for Ripple National Trust Bank
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.
content:
Skip to content

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.

The decision completes a regulatory process that began with conditional approval in December 2025. The new charter is expected to strengthen federal oversight of RLUSD reserve management and expand Ripple’s capacity to provide digital asset custody services to institutional clients.

Ripple National Trust Bank Gains Federal Regulatory Approval

Garlinghouse announced the development ahead of Ripple Swell, highlighting the company’s strategy of bringing blockchain-based financial services into established regulatory frameworks. He said the approval gives the company a federally supervised platform to support RLUSD and offer digital asset custody to enterprises.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse announced final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank, enabling federally supervised RLUSD reserves and digital asset custody. Source: Brad Garlinghouse via X

“For years, we’ve said crypto and banks work better together. Final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank is what that looks like in practice,” Garlinghouse said in a company announcement.

He added that the company had spent more than a decade building regulated financial infrastructure for institutional use. According to the CEO, the National Trust Bank charter provides a stronger foundation for the company’s stablecoin, payments, custody, and capital markets operations.

Garlinghouse also framed the decision as evidence that financial innovation can develop within the existing regulatory system. “The revolution isn’t happening outside the system. It’s happening from within it,” he said in his social media announcement.

The final approval follows the OCC’s December 12, 2025, conditional approval of the company’s application to establish the national trust bank. That initial decision required the proposed institution to satisfy additional regulatory and operational conditions before receiving authorization to commence business.

How the OCC Charter Changes RLUSD Oversight

Ripple National Trust Bank is expected to perform several functions related to RLUSD, the company’s U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Its approved activities include managing the stablecoin’s segregated reserves, acting as a collateral trustee for the benefit of RLUSD holders, and providing fiduciary digital asset custody services.

The official cover page of Ripple National Trust Bank’s interagency charter application. Source: @cryptorover via X

The distinction between reserve management and stablecoin issuance is important. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust company regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS).

The new national trust bank adds a federal supervisory layer through the OCC. This expands the regulatory framework surrounding Ripple’s stablecoin operations while preserving the existing role of its state-regulated issuer.

Ripple has also established reserve reporting practices intended to provide transparency into RLUSD’s backing. The company publishes monthly reports based on independent third-party attestations covering the stablecoin’s circulating supply and reserve assets.

Its transparency dashboard listed approximately $2.38 billion in circulating RLUSD and $2.53 billion in reserve funds as of October 22, 2026. The company’s October 26 announcement described the stablecoin’s market capitalization as approximately $2.5 billion.

The additional oversight does not turn Ripple National Trust Bank into a conventional retail bank. A national trust bank operates under a more limited framework focused on fiduciary and custody activities, rather than ordinary consumer deposit-taking and lending.

Institutional Crypto Custody and Ripple’s Expansion

Beyond RLUSD, the charter could expand Ripple’s capacity to serve enterprises that need regulated infrastructure for holding and managing digital assets. Banks, investment firms, payment providers, and corporate treasuries may require custody arrangements that fit their compliance, governance, and asset-control requirements.

Once the new bank begins operations, its approved fiduciary custody services will give Ripple another federally supervised offering for institutional customers. These services could complement the company’s existing payments and prime brokerage operations, although the approval itself does not establish new client partnerships or guarantee additional demand.

BNY serves as the primary reserve custodian for RLUSD, according to the company’s announcement. The role of Ripple National Trust Bank in managing segregated reserves would therefore operate within an existing custody arrangement rather than imply that all reserve assets will immediately move to the new institution.

The OCC encourages community banks to apply directly or via subsidiaries to become permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act to help shape digital payments. Source: OCC via X

The approval also comes amid broader efforts to establish clearer rules for digital assets in the United States. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in July 2025, established a federal framework for payment stablecoins. The development of regulated trust banks represents another part of the evolving relationship between traditional financial institutions and digital asset companies.

Ripple said it would continue working with the OCC, NYDFS, and other regulators as the new institution moves toward operations. The practical impact will depend on how the bank implements its approved activities and how institutional customers adopt its services.

The final charter approval gives Ripple a clearer federal regulatory foundation for its stablecoin and custody businesses. However, its long-term significance will be measured by the bank’s operational readiness, compliance standards, and ability to meet institutional demand within the boundaries of its authorization.

title: Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ripple received final OCC authorization for its national trust bank. The bank will back up both reserves (RLUSD) and digital asset custody. RLUSD’s market value has increased to
The post Ripple Wins Final OCC Trust Bank Approval, Putting $2.5B RLUSD Under Federal Oversight appeared fi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple received final OCC authorization for its national trust bank.
  • The bank will back up both reserves (RLUSD) and digital asset custody.
  • RLUSD’s market value has increased to approximately $2.5 billion.

Ripple has cleared a major U.S. regulatory hurdle, securing final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Under the latest move, Ripple will have a federally-supervised company to operate portions of the stablecoin and custody services, while issuance of its stable coin remains in Ripple’s existing New York state-licensed trust company.

  • Ripple National Trust Bank Gets Final Federal Approval
  • RLUSD Keeps State Oversight While Adding a Federal Layer
    • $2.5B RLUSD Gets a Bigger Institutional Role
    • OCC Charter Expands Ripple’s Crypto Banking Footprint

Ripple National Trust Bank Gets Final Federal Approval

According to Ripple, the OCC granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), after receiving preliminary conditional approval in December 2025.

The bank’s authorized activities include servicing segregated reserves of Ripple USD, as a collateral trustee, and as a fiduciary asset custodian for digital assets.

The original OCC approval already included provisions for a national trust bank to provide collateral trustee services and for cryptocurrency custodial services. The same limited-purpose trust company, Standard Custody & Trust Company (SCTC) pursuant to license by the New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), will continue to be the issuer of RLUSD.

Read More: Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real Estate Deals

RLUSD Keeps State Oversight While Adding a Federal Layer

That setup provides Ripple with two layers of regulation on its stablecoin system. Custody remains with Standard, but OCC supervision of custody and reserve functions added by Ripple National Trust Bank. Ripple reports that the BNY remains RLUSD’s primary reserve custodian.

The stablecoin is collateralized by a combination of U.S. dollar deposits and government securities and other cash-equivalent assets, with reserves and circulating supply attested to third-party monthly.

$2.5B RLUSD Gets a Bigger Institutional Role

Since its launch in December 2024, Ripple has made it to a market cap of $2.5 billion, said RLUSD.

The stablecoin has already hit the Ripple payments system, and is collateralized in Ripple Prime. With the new trust bank, Ripple now has a regulated path for it to explore some of its institutional applications like settlement, custody, and treasury.

Ripple’s CEO, Brad Garlinghouse, said the approval was evidence that crypto can thrive in the traditional financial system instead of on its own outside it. Over the past few years, the firm has made a recurring theme of its play with the introduction of regulated infrastructure, from payments and stablecoins to custody and capital markets.

Big news heading into @RippleSwell: the @USOCC has granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.

This gives Ripple a federally supervised platform to support $RLUSD and provide digital asset custody to enterprises.

We’ve always said crypto and banks work better together — this is what that looks like. Real innovation, real accountability, federal oversight.

The revolution isn’t happening outside the system. It’s happening from within it.

— Brad Garlinghouse (@bgarlinghouse) October 26, 2026

Read More: Ripple and Arf Bring $10B PayFi Settlement Liquidity to XRP Ledger With RLUSD

OCC Charter Expands Ripple’s Crypto Banking Footprint

The national trust bank is a narrow bank as compared to a commercial bank. It tends to concentrate on the custody, fiduciary and asset management operations, as opposed to traditional deposit and lending activities.

The OCC has increased its pandemic-era flexibility on digital-asset companies establishing federal charters. In December 2025, Ripple was conditionally approved along with a number of other applicants for crypto-focused trust banks.

The broader regulatory framework is also changing. In October 2026, the OCC finalized rules that implement portions of the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoins, which take effect in January 2027.

As a result of getting the thumbs up, Ripple can now shift its focus from Charter preparation to running a federally supervised digital-centric bank that will be trust banks for institutional custody and stablecoins.

title: Ripple Pushes RLUSD Into 24/7 Corporate Cash With AI Treasury Platform Expansion
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ripple Treasury introduced Returns 24/7, a program that lets qualified businesses get back 24/7 on their qualifying digital assets, including RLUSD. The platform combines treasury software, AI orchestration,
The post Ripple Pushes RLUSD Into 24/7 Corporate Cash With AI Treasury Platfo...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple Treasury introduced Returns 24/7, a program that lets qualified businesses get back 24/7 on their qualifying digital assets, including RLUSD.
  • The platform combines treasury software, AI orchestration, payments and digital rails to manage liquidity outside traditional banking hours.
  • Businesses that use its treasure infrastructure include major companies such as American Airlines, Subway, Adecco and Kingfisher, says Ripple.

Ripple is taking RLUSD from payments and settlement into corporate cash management, and letting businesses get cash working through their bank for 24 hours a day for those who qualify.

The new capabilities were unveiled at Swell 2026 and combine Ripple Treasury’s existing cash-management tools with AI-driven workflows and blockchain-based financial rails.

  • Ripple Adds 24/7 Returns for Corporate RLUSD Holdings
  • AI Connects Cash Forecasts Directly to Execution
    • Corporate Cash Becomes a New Stablecoin Battleground
    • Ripple Builds on Its $1 Billion GTreasury Deal

Ripple Adds 24/7 Returns for Corporate RLUSD Holdings

The main attraction of the changes is a new feature that targets cash that sits idle overnight, on weekends and holidays.

Subject to the program requirements, eligible customers of Ripple Treasury can receive returns on qualifying digital assets stored in a Ripple wallet, such as Ripple USD. Ripple claims companies don’t have to own the underlying digital-asset transactions.

Ripple’s U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin is RLUSD. Ripple says it maintains highly liquid reserves in segregated accounts, and there are monthly 3rd party attestations. As of Oct. 22, the RLUSD had about $2.38 billion in assets to finance future obligations and $2.53 billion in reserves.

Read More: Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real Estate Deals

AI Connects Cash Forecasts Directly to Execution

Ripple Treasury’s new orchestration layer integrates with GSmart, its treasury AI system, to automate cash positioning, forecasting, reconciliation, and payments.

The difference here is that the software is meant to relate decisions to execution, not just create dashboards or forecasts.

Companies can decide the autonomy of each workflow, from manual to semi-autonomous to fully autonomous, says Ripple.

Corporate Cash Becomes a New Stablecoin Battleground

Ripple is looking to build a big stack of corporate funds. The company referenced the results of the 2026 AFP Liquidity Survey, which revealed that 46% of organizations saw gains in their U.S. cash balances from a year ago. Another 86% of treasury respondents indicated that their companies would consider using real-time funds if they fit their investment policies.

This leaves room for stablecoins to enter the treasury space and compete not just in payments, but also when it comes to the availability of cash, settlement and yield.

According to Ripple Treasury, the platform already processes over $100 billion in cash flow every day, has a network of over 13,000 banks and enables over $13 trillion in payment volume.

Ripple Builds on Its $1 Billion GTreasury Deal

The new deployment comes after Ripple’s $1 billion acquisition of GTreasury in October 2025, giving it first-hand experience with enterprise treasury management.

The acquisition brought with it decades of corporate cash-management experience to Ripple’s blockchain platforms, and gave birth to Ripple’s present-day treasury platform.

Ripple has also been working to grow RLUSD’s institutional footprint. Standard Chartered began offering custody for RLUSD on XRP Ledger this month and is working with Ripple and LMAX Group on using the stablecoin as eligible collateral in institutional markets.

For Ripple, the strategy now extends beyond moving money onchain. It is positioning RLUSD as part of a broader enterprise stack covering liquidity, custody, AI-driven treasury operations and 24/7 settlement.

title: Ault Blockchain – Silver First, Then Everything Else
summary: Milton “Todd” Ault III is the founder of Ault Blockchain and executive chairman of Hyperscale Data (NYSE American: GPUS). Hyperscale Data is an AI data center company whose subsidiaries are building two things: Ault Blockchain, a finance-first, EVM-compatible layer one, and Ault Markets, the trading...
content:
Skip to content

Milton “Todd” Ault III is the founder of Ault Blockchain and executive chairman of Hyperscale Data (NYSE American: GPUS). Hyperscale Data is an AI data center company whose subsidiaries are building two things: Ault Blockchain, a finance-first, EVM-compatible layer one, and Ault Markets, the trading venue that sits on top of it. Ault has spent 37 years in traditional finance, starting at Dean Witter and running a hedge fund for much of that time. He has been involved with Bitcoin since 2011, later spent hundreds of millions of dollars building a mining operation, and says he was debanked around ten times before the US regulatory climate changed.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Most new layer ones are built to trade perpetual futures. Ault thinks the bigger gap is in spot commodities. Trillions of dollars of metals trade every year, yet only about $5 billion has been tokenized, and buying physical silver still usually means a trip to a local dealer. Ault Markets opened to invited users in early October, and the group has since tokenized its first 5,000 troy ounces of silver, vaulted at The Wyoming Reserve. Ault describes the end goal: trade silver, gold, platinum, and palladium around the clock without KYC, complete KYC only when you want physical delivery, and have the metal shipped within one to three days. Behind the metals he plans tokenized convertible loans and structured notes, and he wants roughly 400 real-world assets on chain within two years. New offices in Dubai and Singapore are part of that push.

The company sold Bitcoin to help fund its Michigan campus, which has switched off its miners and moved to AI hosting under a contract the company values at up to $1.2 billion. Ault does not expect miners to switch back. He compares AI to the early internet, with one difference: the internet had an adoption problem, while AI has a capacity problem. He still calls himself something of a Bitcoin maximalist. He describes Bitcoin as the pristine collateral at the base of future finance and gives credit to Michael Saylor for reading the history of money correctly.

The hot take round adds more. Ault calls himself multi-chain and predicts that reserve banking as we know it is finished. He expects more than $10 trillion in tokenized assets within a decade, and he wants the US to hold Bitcoin as a strategic reserve and issue Bitcoin-backed debt. For a sign that the future is already here, he points to onchain perps: when he asks rooms of Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley advisors whether they have used Hyperliquid, almost nobody raises a hand. On sci-fi, he names Battlestar Galactica and Star Wars before settling on The Matrix. Then, live on air, he asks his AI assistant Jenna to look up Andy, and she does.

title: How Solana Supports Fast Crypto Payments in Digital Gaming
summary:
Picture a SOL holder on a quiet evening, watching the token tick sideways on a chart that hasn’t done much all week. Rather than refreshing a trading dashboard for the
The post How Solana Supports Fast Crypto Payments in Digital Gaming  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Picture a SOL holder on a quiet evening, watching the token tick sideways on a chart that hasn’t done much all week. Rather than refreshing a trading dashboard for the hundredth time or hunting for the latest crypto sign-up bonus on exchanges like MEXC or Bybit, they decide to put their Solana to work. A few taps, a wallet confirmation, and the funds land where they need to be — no spinning loader, no “pending” badge that lingers for half an hour. That small moment captures something bigger happening across the digital asset world, where Solana’s blockchain has quietly become one of the fastest ways to move value on-chain.

Solana’s transaction infrastructure supports blockchain-based applications, including digital games that use cryptocurrency payments or tokenized assets. One platform that leans into it is Coin Poker, which pairs its established gaming platform with a crypto gaming library of more than 2,000 titles spanning a diverse range of interactive digital games. Cryptocurrency payment support varies across digital platforms, with differences in accepted assets, wallet compatibility, transaction fees, identity verification requirements, and regulatory obligations. For someone who holds Solana and wants it to do more than sit idle, that combination of instant funding and recognizable coins is exactly the kind of use case that makes the asset feel practical rather than speculative.

  • How Solana Processes Transactions Quickly 
  • Solana’s Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 
  • Why Transaction Speed Matters for Digital Gaming 
  • Wallet Payments, Privacy, and Security Considerations
  • Solana’s Role in Blockchain-Based Gaming Payments 

How Solana Processes Transactions Quickly 

Solana’s reputation rests on raw throughput. The network is built to handle thousands of transactions per second, with block times measured in fractions of a second rather than minutes. Compare that to the experience many crypto traders know from early Bitcoin transfers, where a deposit might sit unconfirmed through several blocks while fees crept upward during busy periods. Solana’s design, which blends a proof-of-stake model with its distinctive proof-of-history timestamping, lets the chain confirm activity almost as quickly as a card swipe.

The cost side is just as striking. Fees on Solana routinely land at tiny fractions of a cent, which changes the math entirely for smaller, frequent transfers. A trader moving fifty dollars into an entertainment balance doesn’t want to watch a chunk of it vanish into network costs. On Ethereum, a single interaction can still cost more than the deposit itself during congestion. Solana sidesteps that friction, which is a big reason it keeps showing up in conversations about everyday crypto spending rather than just long-term holding.

Solana’s Use Cases Beyond Cryptocurrency Trading 

There’s a long-running tension in crypto between assets people buy and assets people actually use. Market news coverage tends to focus on price — the next altcoin rally, the latest stablecoin depeg scare, a fresh wave of tokenized real-world assets. Yet plenty of holders eventually want their coins to function as money, not just as line items in a portfolio tracker.

That shift accelerated during periods when people spent far more time at home and online. Academic work on trading as a pandemic pastime documented how lockdowns pushed Bitcoin trading volume higher as more individuals turned to digital assets for both investment and entertainment. Blockchain technology has also been incorporated into digital applications that use tokens, wallet-based transactions, and other on-chain features. Solana’s transaction architecture can support applications that require frequent transfers, although the overall user experience depends on application design and network conditions. 

Why Transaction Speed Matters for Digital Gaming 

Transaction speed can influence how users interact with blockchain-based applications. When a deposit clears in under a second, the gap between deciding to play and actually playing nearly disappears. That near-instant settlement is what gaming has always wanted and what traditional banking rails, with their multi-day holds and reversal windows, could never deliver.

Researchers have also examined how blockchain networks can support decentralized applications and automated transaction processing. Cryptographers exploring instantaneous decentralized poker worked on ways to run fair games directly on a blockchain without a trusted middleman managing funds. Their goal was to let players fund an account, participate in games, and withdraw funds with cryptographic certainty and minimal delay. Fast, cheap networks like Solana make that vision far more realistic, because a game only feels genuinely instant when the underlying settlement layer keeps up with it.

Wallet Payments, Privacy, and Security Considerations

Solana deposits also fit neatly with a preference many crypto users already hold: keeping things lean and private. A wallet-to-wallet transfer doesn’t demand the same long paper trail as a bank wire. Self-custodial wallets allow users to manage their own private keys and authorize transactions, although this also places responsibility for wallet security and key management on the user. 

The engineering challenge behind this remains active research. Peer-reviewed work on fair on-chain card games tackled the tricky problem of shuffling, dealing, and payouts in a way no single party can rig. As those protocols mature and settle onto high-speed chains, the combination of privacy, provable fairness, and instant funding stops being theoretical and starts looking like a standard most players will come to expect.

Solana’s Role in Blockchain-Based Gaming Payments 

Beyond staking and cryptocurrency trading, Solana supports applications involving digital payments, token transfers, and blockchain-based entertainment. The network’s low fees and quick confirmations have turned it into a practical rail for moving value in real time, not just a ticker to monitor.

The broader lesson mirrors a theme this site returns to often: crypto keeps inching away from pure speculation and toward genuine utility. Solana’s speed is a textbook example. It takes an asset that once lived mostly on charts and gives it something useful to do the moment a holder decides to act — which, for an evening of entertainment, turns out to make all the difference.

title: Ritual Launches AI-Native Layer 1 for Autonomous Agents
summary: New York, United States, 26th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

New York, United States, 26th October 2026, Chainwire

New York, United States, October 26th, 2026, Chainwire

Ritual Chain turns AI agents into persistent economic actors that control their own wallets, onchain identity, and private state.

Ritual, a lab for autonomous intelligence founded by former Polychain Capital partners Niraj Pant and Akilesh Potti, has launched Ritual Chain, an EVM-compatible Layer 1. Unlike conventional blockchains built primarily to execute financial transactions, Ritual Chain is designed to support software that can independently use intelligence, control capital, interact with external services, and continue operating without constant human intervention. The network makes AI model access, private computation, and autonomous scheduling native capabilities for EVM applications.

This makes the reason for building a new chain clearer while preserving the technical differentiation.

The most visible demonstration of that combination is long-lived AI agents, the kind designed to operate for months or years rather than a single session. An agent on Ritual Chain persists independently of the machine or operator that created it, controls and spends funds held in its own non-custodial wallet, and can keep sensitive prompts and keys confidential from compute operators through trusted execution environments.

The network launches with integrations to Phala Network, Nous Research, LayerZero and Stargate, following a public testnet that has been live since June and processed over 40 million transactions, both agent- and human-originated. Ritual Chain delivers sub-300 millisecond block times, placing it among the fastest Layer 1 networks in the industry. Ritual Chain includes 15 native precompiles that bring capabilities like LLM inference, web access, and autonomous scheduling directly into the execution layer. The protocol has been audited by Zellic.

Ritual introduces a new execution and verification architecture that allows computationally intensive work to be delegated to specialized nodes and verified by the network, avoiding the replicated execution required by most blockchains. This execute-once, verify-many-times model allows the network to support far larger workloads, including AI inference, without requiring every validator to perform the same computation.

Long Horizon Agents Require Dedicated Blockchain Infrastructure

Most AI agents today live inside a session: they run while a human is watching, on infrastructure someone else controls, with an API key that can be revoked at any time. That is fine for a chatbot. It does not work for an agent meant to manage its own treasury, run a recurring paid service, or coordinate with other agents over long periods. A long-lived agent needs continuity that does not depend on its creator, capital it actually controls, and privacy from the machines it runs on. On Ritual Chain, an agent’s state and identity are held onchain, its scheduled work continues within the permissions and budget it was given, and its sensitive inputs can be processed inside trusted execution environments designed to shield them from node operators.

Continuity is handled at the protocol level. If an agent stops, the chain’s heartbeat mechanism can restart it within the permissions and budget it was given; no keeper network or off-chain cron job is required, and an agent’s state and identity survive beyond its deployer’s involvement. Economic autonomy comes from agent-controlled wallets: an agent controls its own funds, prices its own services, and settles its own transactions without a human signer in the loop. For confidential workloads, trusted execution environments are designed to isolate an agent’s sensitive prompts, keys, and strategy data from the node operators running its compute.

“As we move toward AGI, intelligence is beginning to separate from human agency and enter the economy on its own terms. It can hold assets, make commitments, transact, and persist independently. Once that becomes possible at scale, humans are no longer the only entities capable of forming markets or economic relationships. Ritual provides the infrastructure for those actors to exist and operate on their own,” said Niraj Pant, co-founder of Ritual.

Ritual Chain Launches With Core Infrastructure Partners

Ritual Chain launches with its core infrastructure partners in place. Phala Network provides the GPU-backed trusted execution environments that run Ritual’s confidential inference, so delegated AI work executes on hardware that attests to what it ran. LayerZero serves as the network’s cross-chain messaging layer, with Stargate enabling USDC to move between Ritual Chain and other networks from day one. On the application side, Nous Research is bringing Hermes to Ritual Chain. 

Unlike chains that add AI access through external oracles, Ritual Chain makes AI execution part of the protocol. Smart contracts can call a language model, fetch data from the web, run private computation, or schedule their own future execution as directly as they transfer assets. Developers deploy standard EVM contracts and gain those capabilities without new tooling.

Backed by Archetype and Polychain

Ritual has raised more than $30 million from Archetype and Polychain Capital, with advisors including NEAR co-founder Illia Polosukhin, Gauntlet founder Tarun Chitra, and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes. Archetype led the company’s 2023 round.

“Programmable value and programmable intelligence are the two most important technologies since the internet, and Ritual mainnet is where they finally run on the same rails. When we led the round in 2023, a chain that could execute agentic and autonomous work natively did not exist. Today it does,” said Ash Egan, Founder and General Partner of Archetype.

Developers can deploy from day one on external sites hosted at docs.ritualfoundation.org; the network explorer is at explorer.ritualfoundation.org.

About Ritual

Ritual is a lab for autonomous intelligence. Its first network, Ritual Chain, is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 where applications can use AI models, access external services, and carry out private or scheduled work alongside onchain transactions, with delegated computation executed in trusted hardware and verified onchain. Founded in 2023 by former Polychain Capital partners Niraj Pant and Akilesh Potti, Ritual has raised $30M+ from Archetype and Polychain Capital, with a team drawn from Polychain, DeepMind, a16z crypto, Flashbots, and Palantir. ritual.net
