title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind Join UK’s New AI Biosecurity Mission
summary: The UK government has launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab, bringing together OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to strengthen defenses against biological threats and improve AI-powered disease detection and medical research.
content:
Skip to content

The UK government has launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab, bringing together OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to strengthen defenses against biological threats and improve AI-powered disease detection and medical research.

The initiative forms part of the UK’s National AI Biosecurity Initiative. OpenAI and Anthropic have committed up to £200 million combined in AI model credits, computing resources, and access to advanced systems, while Google DeepMind and Basecamp Research will contribute research collaborations and specialized AI biology tools.

The lab aims to detect emerging biological threats earlier and accelerate the development of vaccines, treatments, and other medical countermeasures. The government describes it as the world’s first dedicated AI biosecurity organization.

UK AI Biosecurity Lab Targets Emerging Biological Threats

The AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) will apply advanced AI systems to biological risk assessment, disease surveillance, and emergency preparedness. It will work with government agencies, academic institutions, and life sciences organizations to strengthen the UK’s response to emerging threats.

The UK launched a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind to detect and counter biological threats. Source: Bloomberg via X

AI can accelerate scientific discovery and help researchers identify potential treatments. However, increasingly capable models may also lower barriers to certain forms of harmful biological research, creating additional challenges for public health and national security.

The lab will focus initially on two priorities: improving the early detection of biological threats and accelerating the development and testing of vaccines, treatments, and other medical countermeasures.

Its work will support the UK’s existing biosecurity infrastructure and broader Biological Security Strategy. The aim is to translate advances in AI into practical capabilities that help authorities assess risks and prepare for disease outbreaks.

OpenAI and Anthropic Commit Up to £200 Million

OpenAI and Anthropic have pledged up to £200 million in combined support, primarily through AI model credits, computing resources, trusted access to advanced systems, and technical assistance. These commitments are distinct from direct government funding.

The lab receives £100 million in UK government funding and up to £200 million in AI credits, with support from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Basecamp Research. Source: @Polymarket via X

OpenAI’s contribution includes £100 million in computing and model credits, alongside trusted access to relevant advanced models through its Rosalind Biodefense program. Anthropic has pledged up to £100 million in model credits, model access, and dedicated technical support.

The resources are intended to give researchers access to advanced AI capabilities without requiring the lab to finance equivalent computing and model usage independently.

Google DeepMind will contribute through research collaborations involving its scientists and biosecurity experts, while Basecamp Research will provide AI biology models, technical expertise, and related scientific tools.

The partnerships bring together AI developers, biological researchers, and public-sector specialists to develop capabilities for identifying and responding to biological risks.

UK Expands AI Security Investment Beyond Biosecurity

The lab is part of a wider government package addressing AI safety, cybersecurity, and the economic effects of technological change.

The UK has allocated £165 million to its National AI Biosecurity Initiative, including £100 million for the lab and £65 million for pathogen countermeasures. A further £120 million will go to the AI Security Institute to expand its assessment of advanced AI models and emerging risks.

The UK is investing an additional £120 million in the AI Security Institute, £60 million in a National Cyber Shield, and £70 million in a new NERV Centre to strengthen cybersecurity. Source: @KanishkaNarayan via X

The package also includes £60 million for a National Cyber Shield and £70 million for a vulnerability center to strengthen cyber threat detection and identify weaknesses affecting critical systems.

Additional measures target domestic AI development and economic adaptation. These include £60 million in extra funding for the Sovereign AI Fund, £23 million for the AI Economics Institute to examine AI’s effects on jobs and productivity, and £30 million for partnerships with regional mayors to support AI adoption by businesses and public services.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has framed the government’s approach around developing safe AI while protecting national security and technological independence.

Independent Organization to Coordinate Research

The AI Biosecurity Lab will operate as an independent, non-profit organization. Its structure is intended to attract specialists from industry and academia while allowing research teams to work at the pace of advanced AI and biotechnology development.

A scientific advisory committee comprising experts from academia, industry, and the third sector will guide its work. The lab will also collaborate with public institutions responsible for health security, animal and plant health, defense research, and medicines regulation.

These partnerships are designed to connect AI research with the organizations responsible for monitoring biological threats, evaluating risks, and coordinating emergency responses. The lab will also work with international partners where appropriate.

AI Biosecurity Becomes a National Security Priority

The initiative reflects a growing challenge for policymakers: AI can accelerate scientific discovery, but its expanding capabilities may also introduce biological risks that require new safeguards.

By combining public funding with access to advanced AI systems and specialist biological research, the UK aims to improve its ability to identify threats and develop countermeasures. The program also links AI safety with broader priorities, including cybersecurity and domestic technology development.

The lab’s effectiveness will depend on whether its research produces reliable, practical tools for public health and security agencies. Detection systems must provide useful warnings, while AI-assisted scientific findings require appropriate testing and validation before they can guide real-world decisions.

The launch establishes the lab’s funding, partnerships, and initial objectives. Its longer-term impact will depend on the capabilities it develops and how effectively public institutions use them.

For the UK, the immediate goal is to harness advanced AI for biological defense while supporting beneficial scientific research. The collaboration with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Basecamp Research places the new organization at the intersection of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and national security.

content:
Key Takeaways:

On October 26th, 2026, Soneium announced its next stage of development, which involves tokenizing IP and new funding mechanisms for entertainment endeavors. Over 250 applications are already available on the network for music, games, anime, movies, and collectibles.

1/ 💿 Soneium: The Onchain Entertainment Economy.

Today we introduce Tokenized IP and our plan to issue $SONEIUM, an ecosystem-native token that connects our global community. 🧵👇 https://t.co/jMwv9qoit3

— Soneium 💿 (@soneium) October 26, 2026

  • $SONEIUM to Connect Soneium’s Entertainment Ecosystem
  • Tokenized IP Targets Entertainment Investments
    • Blockchain Infrastructure for IP Rights and Royalties

$SONEIUM to Connect Soneium’s Entertainment Ecosystem

To connect creators, IP holders, app makers, fans, and investors, Soneium will launch $SONEIUM as a native ecosystem token. The project targets to create an on-chain entertainment economy that enables communities to fund and join the growth of creative projects.

But, Soneium has not announced the token supply or TGE date. More information will be released shortly.

Read More: Raydium LaunchLab Unlocks Any Token Pair on Solana

Tokenized IP Targets Entertainment Investments

The programme consists of three programmes: IP Tokens, IP Vault and Tokenised IP Bonds. IP Tokens may be for creators, studios or individual entertainment properties, with IP Vault serving to unlock opportunities like music catalog funds. Tokenized IP Bonds will be targeting entertainment business income, such as concert royalties.

The first announced IP Token is the character from Super State Holdings, Moriusa, who is based in Tokyo. The project includes plans to venture into licensing investments, animated short films and merchandise.

Soneium will also be working with DayOneDream to bring K-pop concert-business royalties on-chain, where artists such as BTOB and LEE CHAE YEON are included. The Soneium Portal will be the key discovery and interaction platform for this, and the Startale App will offer access to the broader ecosystem.

Blockchain Infrastructure for IP Rights and Royalties

Soneium is focused on building an Onchain IP Architecture: IP Registry, which supports all records of creative work and ownership information, IP Graph, which maps the relations between original and derivative creations, and IP Execution Layer, which automates the licensing and royalty payment process using smart contracts.

The network also offers ERC-8432, a future Ethereum standard that will facilitate application and AI agent licensing. The new system is designed to support creators in managing the use of their content in this evolving landscape of AI-generated content.

Soneium states that it’s not an alternative to copyright laws, but an addition. Successful adoption of the initiative will rely on development of the token, products and infrastructure to license the new offering.

Robinhood Chain DEX Volume Pushes Toward $30 Billion

According to the DefiLlama data, Robinhood Chain has realized around $29.9 billion over the last 30 days in DEX trading volumes and its 24-h trading business is around the $490m mark recently. They can move on a chain with speed due to the tracking of rolling activity on the chain.

Uniswap is still the biggest contributor, with over $24 billion worth of volume on its decentralized exchange (DEX) in a single snapshot over the last 30 days. Other protocols include players from Fables, RamsesX, Metric and some smaller protocols.

The company’s mainnet strategy announcement in July centered around tokenizing stocks, decentralized finance, and introducing financial products to the global audience. Robinhood’s aim was to bridge the gap between traditional brokerage operations and onchain trading markets, the company said.

The post CoinDCX Confirms $15.99M USDT Loss After Failed Sweep Hit Old Crypto Wallets appeared first on ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • CoinDCX announced a $15.99M USDT loss from the old wallet infrastructure in the last contaminated security event impacting the platform in 2025.
  • The exchange said that an automated sweeping program malfunctioned, and that deposits were made at an old address and then lost.
  • Customer balances, withdrawals and active trading systems did not get affected, said CoinDCX of the loss suffered by it.

Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX has confirmed losing nearly $16 million in USDT after funds accumulated in wallet infrastructure the company had already retired following an earlier security breach.

This revelation immediately follows on-chain research of suspicious transfers from addresses associated with CoinDCX, which questioned the logic of receiving deposits while wallets allegedly deemed “deprecated”.

  • CoinDCX Says Failed Wallet Sweep Caused $15.99M Loss
  • Old Deposit Addresses Were Still Receiving Crypto
    • On-Chain Data Challenged the ‘Deprecated Wallet’ Label

CoinDCX Says Failed Wallet Sweep Caused $15.99M Loss

According to CoinDCX, they noticed unusual transactions on October 21 and also spied on unusual fund transfers through blockchain information and community reports.

During the investigation, it was revealed that the activity had an impact on old operating wallet infrastructure that had been affected in the July 2025 incident. A backend service which used to sweep incoming deposits on those addresses into secure CoinDCX wallets went offline for a period, causing coins to pool there.

The loss of USDT was CoinDCX’s loss of 15.99 million USDT, which the exchange reported that it covered. The exchange has stated that their existing wallets and trading systems are not impacted. The company reported trading and deposits and withdrawals were seamless, and assets held by users were still demand-deposited in segregated cold-wallet custody.

Read More: Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After $2.7M Exploit Tied to Unauthorized Token Minting

Old Deposit Addresses Were Still Receiving Crypto

Despite providing notice to update the deposit address, some users are continuing to send coins to older deposit addresses, CoinDCX said.

Its recovery system was divided into two parts: when the funds were sent to an old wallet, users were credited, and a subsequent automated service transferred them to the main secure wallets of CoinDCX.

The expensive incident highlighted the problems with retaining access to previous compromised wallet infrastructure. If the sweeping process fails, deposits may stay in addresses whose security exposure is known.

On-Chain Data Challenged the ‘Deprecated Wallet’ Label

Blockchain researchers have raised questions about the workings of the less active wallets. According to Bitquery, one address held approximately $15.82 million of USDT and the company tracked 15.99 million USDT in 40 CoinDCX-related Tron wallets. It was a routine deposit-related operation through its investigation up to the day of the incident.

Additionally, approximately $9.63 million was traced to addresses that were linked to Binance, OKX and Gate across a period of about 18 hours. CoinDCX has not responded in public about the source of the unauthorized party unlocking these funds.

The authentication was made just days after CoinDCX CEO Sumit Gupta challenged the initial breach reports.

The flagged addresses were from infrastructure breached in 2025 and Gupta had said that the new ones were a “false alarm” in terms of concerns. Later, CoinDCX has publicly admitted that it has been still interacting with those addresses, which were handling its own deposits.
